passage.title: How Botanical Gardens Use Wood Libraries
passage.text:
When visitors stroll through a botanical garden or natural history museum, pressed leaves and dried blossoms in herbarium cabinets usually come to mind as plant collections. Tucked away in climate-controlled basements from Kew Gardens in London to Kyoto and Madison, Wisconsin, however, researchers curate a lesser-known archive that looks like a carpenter's dream bookshelf: thousands of polished rectangular blocks of wood shelved spine-out like hardcover novels, known as a "xylarium."

Carved from documented trees collected around the globe over the past two centuries, each block records a species' unique cellular architecture. Slice a sliver of wood thinner than tissue paper and place it under a microscope, and its water-conducting vessels, rays, and growth rings form a fingerprint as distinctive as human DNA—even decades after a tree was felled and turned into furniture or flooring.

That anatomical library now plays a frontline role against illegal logging, one of the world's most destructive wildlife crimes. Rare tropical rosewoods, mahoganies, and ebonies protected by international treaties look nearly identical to legal plantation timber once sawn into smooth planks and stacked inside shipping containers. Customs officers at ports used to rely on paper export certificates that smugglers easily forged.

By training portable machine-vision cameras and chemical spectrometers on verified xylarium blocks, wood anatomists have given border inspectors field tools that identify protected tree species on the dock within minutes.

Old museum blocks have helped art historians and luthiers too—dating medieval oak panels and matching repair wood for historic bridges—proving that carefully cataloged specimens gain unexpected value long after they are collected.

items.prompt: How can scientists identify a tree species from a tiny slice of wood decades after it was cut?
choices: Every tree trunk has its Latin name written naturally inside the bark.
Protected hardwood species are much denser than common oak.
Each species has a distinct microscopic pattern of vessels, rays, and rings.
Fresh leaves keep growing out of dry furniture planks.

保護樹種がすべてナラ材より重いわけではない。
第2段落の顕微鏡レベルの細胞構造の特徴と一致。
乾燥した家具材から葉は生えない。
items.translation: 伐採から何十年も経った木片からでも科学者が樹種を特定できるのはなぜですか。

passage.title: How Botanical Gardens Use Wood Libraries
passage.text:
When visitors stroll through a botanical garden or natural history museum, pressed leaves and dried blossoms in herbarium cabinets usually come to mind as plant collections. That anatomical library now plays a frontline role against illegal logging, one of the world's most destructive wildlife crimes. Rare tropical rosewoods, mahoganies, and ebonies protected by international treaties look nearly identical to legal plantation timber once sawn into smooth planks and stacked inside shipping containers. Customs officers at ports used to rely on paper export certificates that smugglers easily forged.

items.prompt: One reason port customs officers previously struggled to catch illegally logged rare timber was that
choices: rare timber was usually mixed into crates of paper pulp.
customs checkpoints lacked scales to weigh timber shipments.
international forestry agreements protected only unprocessed logs with bark attached.
sawn planks of protected trees look very similar to legal timber, and paper certificates could be faked.
items.explanation: look nearly identical to legal plantation timber once sawn into smooth planks ... paper export certificates that smugglers easily forgedとある。
distractorReasons: 紙パルプに混ぜられていたからではない。
重量計がなかったからではない。
丸太だけが保護対象だったからではない。
第3段落の製材後の識別困難・書類偽造問題と一致。
items.translation: かつて港の税関職員が違法伐採された希少材を見抜くのに苦労していたのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: How have xylarium collections strengthened port inspections recently?
choices: Verified specimens were used to train portable cameras and spectrometers that identify protected wood in minutes.
Customs regulations now restrict tropical hardwood imports to certified pine plantations.
Port inspectors ship thin plank cross-sections to overseas laboratories for rapid review.
Dockside officers soak wood shavings in color-changing chemical solutions before unloading.
items.explanation: By training portable machine-vision cameras and chemical spectrometers on verified xylarium blocks ... identify protected tree species on the dock within minutes.とある。
distractorReasons: 第4段落のAI画像認識カメラ・分光器の訓練と現場投入の説明に一致。
輸入木材を認証植林マツだけに制限したわけではない。
海外研究機関への郵送では数週間〜数か月かかっていた課題を現地機器で解決した。
埠頭でおがくずに変色試薬をかける方法ではない。
items.translation: 近年、木材標本コレクションは港での検査をどのように強化しましたか。

items.prompt: Volunteers distributed bottled water and crackers to (     ) waiting at the shelter.
items.explanation: 避難所で待っている「住民たち」に水とクラッカーを配ったresidents。
distractorReasons: monumentsは記念碑。
incidentsは出来事・事件。
ingredientsは材料。
residentsは住民・居住者。shelterと合致。
items.translation: ボランティアたちは避難所で待機している住民にペットボトルの水とクラッカーを配りました。

items.prompt: In (     ) of the chilly wind, over three hundred runners joined the charity relay.
items.explanation: in spite of ... で「…にもかかわらず」（＝despite）。冷たい風にもかかわらず300人以上のランナーが参加した。
distractorReasons: in spite ofで〜にもかかわらず。
in front ofは〜の前に。
instead ofは1語で〜の代わりに。
in terms ofは〜の点では。
items.translation: 冷たい風が吹いていたにもかかわらず、300人以上のランナーがチャリティーリレーに参加しました。

items.prompt: To prevent mold in June, open closet doors often to improve air (     ).
items.explanation: 6月のカビを防ぐため、クローゼットの扉をよく開けて空気の「循環・風通し」を良くするair circulation。
distractorReasons: air circulationで空気の循環・通気。moldを防ぐ文脈に合致。
permissionは「許可」で文脈に合わない。
benefitは「利点・恩恵」で文脈に合わない。
equipmentは「設備・機材」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 6月にカビを防ぐには、クローゼットの扉をこまめに開けて風通しを良くしましょう。

items.prompt: Grandpa still goes cycling every morning; he is young at (     ) at eighty.
items.explanation: young at heartで「気持ち（心）が若々しい」。80歳でも毎朝サイクリングに出かけるほど気が若い。
distractorReasons: headは使わない。
handはat hand（手元に・間近に）。
young at heartで気持ちは若い（定型句）。
mindは使わない。
items.translation: 祖父は今でも毎朝サイクリングに出かけており、80歳にして気持ちがとても若々しいです。

items.prompt:
A: Did you happen to bring back the folding umbrella I lent you?
B: Oh, I'm sorry! I meant to pack it, but it completely slipped my (     ).
items.explanation: slip one's mindで「うっかり忘れる・記憶から抜け落ちる」。昨日傘を返すつもりだったのにすっかり忘れてしまった。
distractorReasons: slip my mindでうっかり忘れる（定型句）。
brainは使わない。
senseは使わない。
sightは使わない。
items.translation: A：貸していた折りたたみ傘、もしかして持ってきてくれた？ B：あ、ごめん！かばんに入れるつもりだったのに、うっかり頭から抜けてしまっていたよ。

items.prompt: Without the lighthouse beam, the boat might have struck the (     ) reef.
items.explanation: 灯台の光がなければ、船は「浅瀬の」暗礁に乗り上げていたかもしれないshallow reef。
distractorReasons: mellowは芳醇な・穏やかな。
hollowは空洞の。
narrowは幅の狭い。
shallow reefで水面近くの浅い岩礁。struckと合致。
items.translation: 灯台の光がなかったら、その船は浅瀬の岩礁に衝突していたかもしれません。

items.prompt: All summer interns are expected to dress neatly and be (     ) for morning briefings.
items.explanation: 朝の打ち合わせに「時間を守る（遅れない）」ことが求められるbe punctual for ...。
distractorReasons: frequentは「頻繁な」で文脈に合わない。
punctualは時間に正確な。morning briefingsと合致。
urgentは「緊急の」で文脈に合わない。
accurateは「正確な」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 夏季インターン生は全員、身だしなみを整え、朝の打ち合わせの時間を厳守することが求められます。

items.prompt:
A: Both teams finished with twelve points.
B: Yes, so the trophy was decided on goal (     ).
items.explanation: 両チームが勝ち点12で並んだため、優勝トロフィーは「得失点差（goal difference）」で決まった。
distractorReasons: goal differenceで得失点差。
featureは「特徴」で文脈に合わない。
climateは「気候」で文脈に合わない。
purposeは「目的」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: A：両チームとも勝ち点12で並んだね。 B：ええ、だから優勝は得失点差で決まりました。

items.prompt: Please attach a return address label just in case the parcel cannot be (     ).
items.explanation: 万一小包が相手に「配達されない」場合に備えて返送先住所ラベルを貼るcannot be delivered。
distractorReasons: expandedは「拡大された」で文脈に合わない。
preservedは「保存された」で文脈に合わない。
deliver a parcelの受動態be delivered。
wrappedは「包まれた」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 万一その小包が配達できない場合に備えて、差出人住所のラベルを貼っておいてください。

items.prompt: Judging (     ) the dark clouds gathering in the west, a thunderstorm is approaching.
items.explanation: judging from ... で「…から判断すると」（慣用分詞構文）。西に集まる暗雲から判断すると雷雨が近づいている。
distractorReasons: intoは使わない。
Judging from ... で〜から判断すると（byも可）。
withは使わない。
overは使わない。
items.translation: 西の空に集まっている黒い雲から判断すると、雷雨が近づいています。

items.prompt: Our teacher warned us that mixing those two cleaners gives (     ) toxic gas.
items.explanation: give off (gas / smell / light)でガスや匂い・光を「発する・放出する」。2つの洗剤を混ぜると有毒ガスが出る。
distractorReasons: give awayは無料で配る・秘密を漏らす。
give inは屈する。
give off gasでガスを発生させる。
give upはあきらめる。
items.translation: あの2種類の洗剤を混ぜると有毒なガスが出ると、先生が注意してくれました。

items.prompt: You can count (     ) Haruna to stay calm whenever technical trouble hits the stage.
items.explanation: count on＋人＋to doで「人が〜してくれると頼りにする・当てにする」。舞台で機材トラブルが起きてもハルナなら落ち着いて対処してくれると頼りにできる。
distractorReasons: inはcount A in（Aを仲間に入れる）。
atは使わない。
forは使わない。
count on A to doでAを頼りにする。
items.translation: 舞台で機材トラブルが起きても、ハルナなら落ち着いて対応してくれると頼りにできます。

items.prompt: The ceramic cup slipped out of my soapy hands and broke (     ) half a dozen pieces.
items.explanation: break into piecesで「粉々に（いくつもの破片に）割れる」。石けんのついた手から滑って6つほどの破片に割れた。
distractorReasons: amongは間で。
overは越えて。
ontoは〜の上へ。
broke into ... piecesで〜個のかけらに割れた。

items.prompt: This pass is valid for three days, (     ) tourists to stop on two islands.
items.explanation: コンマの後ろで前文の内容を受け、「それによって観光客が2つの島に立ち寄れるようにしている」と結果・付帯状況を表す分詞構文allowing。

allowing＋目的語＋to doの分詞構文。

接続詞なしに定形動詞allowsは続けられない。

distractorReasons: hadなら過去分詞realizedが必要。
tasted（過去）と時制を合わせるためdoesは不可。

items.prompt:
A: Excuse me. Can I take the 9:10 cable car down if fog rolls in earlier than forecast?
B: (     ) Your round-trip ticket works on any return car today.
A: Good to know—that gives us peace of mind!
choices: Fog is banned on this mountain.
No, tickets are only good next month.
Cable cars run under the ocean.
Yes, there's no fixed return time.
items.explanation: 往復券は本日のどの帰りの便にも使えますよと説明しているので、帰りの便の時刻指定はありませんから大丈夫ですと答える。

海底ケーブルカーではない。

passage.title: Why Manhole Covers Are Almost Always Round
passage.text:
Walk down almost any city street in the world, and the heavy cast-iron plates covering underground sewer and utility shafts share one unmistakable shape: they are round. Meanwhile, sidewalk grates for rainwater, subway ventilation panels, and telecom curb boxes are often rectangular. That contrast is no accident of tradition—civil engineers settled on circular manhole covers for hard-headed safety and practical reasons.

Consider what happens when workers lift a fifty-kilogram rectangular lid to climb down a ladder. Turned diagonally, a rectangle is narrower across its short side than across its corner-to-corner diagonal, meaning a careless slip could send the heavy iron plate plunging edge-first onto a technician below. (21), a circle has the exact same diameter at every angle, so a round cover resting on an inner lip cannot fall through its opening.

Round lids simplify manufacturing and street work too. Foundries can turn circular rims smoothly on a lathe, workers never have to rotate a heavy cover to match corners when putting it back, and one worker can roll a round plate on its edge like a wheel instead of straining their back. Geometry here quietly protects (22).
passage.translation: 世界中のどの街路を歩いても、下水道や地下配管の縦坑をふさぐ重い鋳鉄製のマンホールの蓋には「丸い」という共通点があります。一方、歩道の雨水ますや地下鉄の換気口には四角い蓋もよく使われています。これには土木工学上の明確な安全・実用上の理由があります。重さ50キロの四角い蓋を外して作業員がはしごを降りる場面を考えてみましょう。長方形や正方形は対角線の長さのほうが短辺より長いため、斜めに傾けると枠をすり抜けて下の作業員の上に落下する危険があります。対照的に円はどの角度で測っても直径が完全に同じであり、ひと回り狭い受け枠の上に載せる構造にすれば丸い蓋は物理的に(21)のです。さらに旋盤で精密に加工しやすく、戻すときに向きを合わせる手間もなく、車輪のように転がして運べるため腰も痛めません。単純な幾何学が(22)の両方を静かに守っているのです。

passage.title: Preparing for the Saturday Riverbank Reed Cutting
passage.text:
From: Kasumigaura Wetland Conservation Group
To: High School Volunteer Participants
Subject: Glove rules and parking change for Saturday's reed-cutting morning

Dear student volunteers,
Thank you for signing up for our annual winter reed cutting this Saturday, January 24 (9:00 a.m. – 11:30 a.m.)! Harvesting dry winter reeds lets spring sunlight warm the shallow water so reed warblers and native minnows thrive, and local craftspeople weave the bundled stalks into traditional summer blinds (sudare).

Dry reed leaves have microscopic silica edges sharp enough to slice thin cotton knit gloves. Please wear thick leather work gloves or rubber-coated gardening gloves—we have twenty extra pairs at the tent if you don't own any.

Because bridge repairs closed the North Lot, all school vans must drop students off at the South Boat Ramp instead.

Coordinator, Wetland Group
passage.translation: 霞ヶ浦湿地保全会から高校生ボランティア参加者へのメール。今週土曜1月24日（午前9時〜11時30分）の冬のヨシ刈りへの参加感謝。枯れた冬のヨシを刈り取ることで春の日差しが浅瀬に届いてヨシキリや在来小魚が育ちやすくなり、刈り取った茎束は地元の職人が伝統的な夏のすだれに編み上げる。乾いたヨシの葉には薄い綿の軍手を切り裂くほど鋭い微細なケイ酸の縁があるため、厚手の革手袋またはゴム張り園芸手袋を着用すること（持っていない人向けにテントに予備20双あり）。橋の補修で北駐車場が閉鎖中のため、学校の送迎バンはすべて南ボートスロープで乗降すること。

passage.title: How Hospital Gardens Speed Patient Recovery
passage.text:
Throughout much of the mid-twentieth century, modern hospital architecture prioritized sterile efficiency above all else. Landscaped courtyards that once surrounded nineteenth-century infirmaries were paved over for parking decks and diagnostic wings, leaving patient rooms facing blank brick walls or air-conditioning shafts.

A turning point arrived in 1984 when environmental psychologist Roger Ulrich examined ten years of surgical recovery charts at a suburban Pennsylvania hospital. Patients recovering from identical gallbladder operations had been assigned randomly to rooms along one corridor: half looked out on a small stand of deciduous trees, while the other half faced a plain brown brick wall. Patients with the tree view requested significantly fewer strong painkillers, reported lower anxiety to nurses, and went home nearly a full day sooner on average.

Follow-up clinical studies in Japan, Sweden, and the United States confirmed that visual and physical contact with greenery lowers stress hormones such as cortisol and steadies heart rate—not only in patients, but also among exhausted ICU nurses and family caregivers taking ten-minute breaks.

Today, architects design "healing gardens" onto hospital rooftops and inner courtyards with careful medical input. Smooth, glare-free paths accommodate wheelchairs and IV poles safely; fragrant herbs and seasonal blossoms help stroke patients rebuild sensory orientation, while toxic or heavy-pollen plants are excluded near allergy wards.

Greenery cannot replace skilled surgeons or antibiotics, of course, yet restoring nature to hospital grounds treats the human nervous system alongside the illness.
passage.translation: 20世紀半ばの近代病院建築は何よりも無菌的な効率性を優先し、かつて療養院を囲んでいた中庭は立体駐車場や検査棟に姿を変え、病室の窓の前には無機質なレンガ壁や空調ダクトが並ぶようになりました。転機となったのは1984年、環境心理学者のロジャー・ウルリッヒがペンシルベニア州の病院で10年分の胆嚢手術後の回復カルテを調べた研究です。同じ廊下で無作為に割り振られた病室のうち、落葉樹の木立が見える部屋の患者は茶色いレンガ壁に面した患者に比べ、強い鎮痛剤の要請が有意に少なく、不安も低く、平均で丸1日近く早く退院していたのです。その後の日本やスウェーデン、米国での臨床研究でも、緑に触れることが患者だけでなく疲弊したICU看護師や付き添い家族のストレスホルモン（コルチゾール）や心拍数を落ち着かせることが裏づけられました。今日では車椅子や点滴スタンドでも安全に通れる無反射の園路や感覚リハビリを助ける香草を備えつつ、アレルギー病棟近くでは花粉の多い植物を避けるなど、医学的知見を取り入れた屋上・中庭の「ヒーリングガーデン」が設計されています。緑が外科医や抗菌薬の代わりになるわけではありませんが、病院に自然を取り戻すことは病気と同時に人間の神経系をも癒やしてくれるのです。

items.prompt: What recovery outcomes were observed in patients whose rooms looked out onto trees?
choices: They spent thirty minutes longer walking outdoors during afternoon rehabilitation.

They reported higher satisfaction with hospital meals and nursing communication.
items.explanation: requested significantly fewer strong painkillers, reported lower anxiety to nurses, and went home nearly a full day sooner on averageとある。

items.translation: 木々が見える病室に入った患者にはどのような回復上の結果が見られましたか。

passage.title: How Hospital Gardens Speed Patient Recovery
passage.text:
Throughout much of the mid-twentieth century, modern hospital architecture prioritized sterile efficiency above all else. Landscaped courtyards that once surrounded nineteenth-century infirmaries were paved over for parking decks and diagnostic wings, leaving patient rooms facing blank brick walls or air-conditioning shafts.

A turning point arrived in 1984 when environmental psychologist Roger Ulrich examined ten years of surgical recovery charts at a suburban Pennsylvania hospital. Patients recovering from identical gallbladder operations had been assigned randomly to rooms along one corridor: half looked out on a small stand of deciduous trees, while the other half faced a plain brown brick wall. Patients with the tree view requested significantly fewer strong painkillers, reported lower anxiety to nurses, and went home nearly a full day sooner on average.

Follow-up clinical studies in Japan, Sweden, and the United States confirmed that visual and physical contact with greenery lowers stress hormones such as cortisol and steadies heart rate—not only in patients, but also among exhausted ICU nurses and family caregivers taking ten-minute breaks.

Today, architects design "healing gardens" onto hospital rooftops and inner courtyards with careful medical input. Smooth, glare-free paths accommodate wheelchairs and IV poles safely; fragrant herbs and seasonal blossoms help stroke patients rebuild sensory orientation, while toxic or heavy-pollen plants are excluded near allergy wards.

Greenery cannot replace skilled surgeons or antibiotics, of course, yet restoring nature to hospital grounds treats the human nervous system alongside the illness.

passage.title: Borrowing More Than Books
passage.text:
A small library wanted to attract residents who rarely borrowed books. Instead of expanding its shelves, it began lending useful household objects, including a sewing machine and a set of gardening tools. The staff hoped that residents could try an object before deciding whether to buy one. People could also borrow items they needed only occasionally.

At first, the library accepted almost every donated object. This created an unexpected problem. Some items were missing parts, while others required repairs that the staff could not perform. The service soon became difficult to manage. The library therefore introduced a rule: every object had to be inspected before it was accepted. (18), donations became easier to handle, even though the library received fewer of them.

Another concern was that borrowers might return objects late. The library considered charging large fines, but staff worried this would discourage people from trying the service. Instead, borrowers received a reminder a day before an item was due. If they needed more time, they could request an extension unless someone else was waiting. The library found that clear communication was (19).

The service is still small. Staff have not claimed that it will replace shopping or solve all the town's waste problems. However, residents have started discussing which objects could usefully be shared. For the library, one important result has been (20). People who had never met now exchange advice about using and repairing the objects they borrow.
passage.translation: ある図書館は読書以外の利用者を呼び込もうと、ミシンや園芸道具など家庭用品の貸出を始めました。購入前に試したり、時々しか使わない物を借りたりできます。最初はほぼすべての寄贈品を受け入れたため、部品不足や修理不能の物が集まり、管理が難しくなりました。受入前の点検を義務化すると、(18)、数は減っても扱いやすくなりました。返却遅延には高額罰金でなく前日通知と、次の予約がない場合の延長で対応し、明確な連絡が(19)と分かりました。小規模な制度で買物の代替や廃棄物問題の全面解決は主張していませんが、共有に役立つ物について住民が話し始めました。重要な成果は(20)で、初対面の人同士が使い方や修理の助言を交換しています。

passage.title: A Sign That Needed Testing
passage.text:
Visitors to a nature reserve were often confused at a junction where two walking paths separated. One route led to a lake, while the other climbed a steep hill. To solve the problem, the reserve installed a large map. The staff were confident that a detailed map would provide all the information visitors needed.

However, volunteers noticed that many people still asked for directions. They interviewed visitors and learned that the map included many small paths but did not clearly show where the viewer was standing. The additional detail had made the map (21). The staff had thought about the whole reserve, while visitors needed to make one immediate choice.

A designer suggested placing a simple sign at the junction. It showed two arrows, the names of the destinations, and the walking time for each route. Before installing the final sign, the staff tested a temporary version for two weekends. They asked volunteers to record how often visitors stopped to ask questions. The number fell considerably. (22), fewer people accidentally began the steep route.

The detailed map was not removed. It remained useful near the entrance, where visitors could plan a longer walk. The project showed that good information is not always the largest amount of information. What matters is (23). The same person may need a broad overview at the start of a visit and a short, clear instruction at a junction.
passage.translation: 自然保護区の分岐点で来訪者が迷うため、職員は詳しい大きな地図を設置しました。しかし質問は減りません。聞き取りでは、小道は多く載っているのに現在地が不明確でした。詳細の追加が地図を(21)していたのです。職員は保護区全体、来訪者は目の前の選択を考えていました。デザイナーは矢印二つ、行き先、所要時間だけの標識を提案。仮設版を2週末試し、質問回数が大幅に減りました。(22)、誤って急な道へ進む人も減りました。詳しい地図は不要になったわけでなく、長い散策の計画を立てる入口で活用されています。情報は多ければよいのでなく、(23)ことが重要です。同じ人でも入口では全体像、分岐では簡明な指示が必要になります。

passage.title: A New Plan for the Exhibition
passage.text:
From: Elena Brooks, Project Leader
To: Student Exhibition Team
Subject: Final arrangements

Dear team,
Thank you for preparing the exhibition on the history of our neighborhood. After looking through your work, the community center has agreed to lend us its main hall. This will allow us to display larger photographs than we could in the school corridor. However, the hall is available for only one weekend, so we must finish setting up by Friday evening and remove everything on Sunday after closing.

We originally planned to borrow display boards from the town office. Unfortunately, they are needed for another event. The center has offered lightweight stands instead. These cannot hold heavy objects, so please do not bring the old tools you collected. Use photographs of them, with short explanations of what they were used for. Your interviews with residents can still be played through the small speakers.

Please send your final captions to me by Monday. I will check them for unclear dates and names, not change your choice of topics. If a resident has asked not to be named, use a description such as "a former shop owner." We have permission to show the donated photographs during the exhibition, but not to post them on social media.

I also need two volunteers to welcome visitors on Saturday morning. You do not have to know every part of local history. Your main task will be to explain the arrangement of the exhibition and direct visitors to the appropriate section. Please reply by tomorrow if you can help.

Elena
passage.translation: 地域史の展示チームへの連絡。学校廊下より大きな写真を展示できる公民館ホールを借りられるが、使用は1週末だけなので金曜夜までに設営し、日曜閉館後に撤去する。当初の展示ボードは別の催しで使うため軽量スタンドに変更。重い古い道具は持ち込まず用途説明付き写真を使う。住民へのインタビューはスピーカーで再生可能。キャプションは月曜までに提出し、担当者は日付や名前の不明点を点検するがテーマは変えない。匿名希望者は「元商店主」などとする。写真は会場展示のみ許可され、SNS投稿は禁止。土曜朝の受付を2名募集。地域史全体の知識でなく展示構成の案内が主な仕事で、参加できる人は翌日までに返信する。

choices: Specialists refused to visit the city.

passage.title: Keeping Track of City Trees
passage.text:
On a summer afternoon, a tree-lined street can feel quite different from a nearby road without shade. Trees also provide places for birds and insects to live. Yet city officials often have incomplete information about the trees they are responsible for. Paper records may be old, and different departments may keep separate lists. This can make it difficult to decide where care is most urgently needed.

In one city, a group of residents offered to help create a shared tree record. Volunteers walked along public streets and entered basic information into a mobile form. They recorded each tree's location, took a photograph, and noted visible signs of damage. They were not asked to judge whether a tree was safe. That decision remained the responsibility of trained specialists.

The first month produced thousands of entries, but some were unreliable. A tree near a street corner might be recorded by two teams, while a photograph taken from far away might show the wrong tree. Rather than simply count the entries, the project leader introduced a checking stage. Teams compared neighboring records, and specialists reviewed reports of possible disease. Each confirmed tree received a single identification number.

The resulting map changed how the city planned its work. Officials had previously responded mainly to requests from residents. However, some neighborhoods made many requests while others made few, even when their trees were in poor condition. The new record allowed officials to compare areas more fairly. It also revealed streets where there were very few trees at all.

The project did not mean that every neighborhood could immediately receive new trees. Planting requires money, and there must be enough space underground for roots as well as above ground for branches. In some streets, water pipes and cables limited the available space. Officials had to explain why a request could not always be accepted.

For volunteers, the main lesson was that collecting information was only the beginning. The value of the record depended on checking it, keeping it current, and using it to answer practical questions. The group now revisits a different area each month. Its members hope that a record built through public participation will remain useful because people understand both its purpose and its limits.
passage.translation: 木陰のある街路は暑い午後にも涼しく感じられ、生き物の場所にもなります。しかし行政の樹木記録は古く、部署ごとに分かれ、必要な手入れの優先順位をつけにくいことがあります。ある市では住民が所在地、写真、目に見える損傷を記録しました。安全性の判断は専門家に残しました。当初は重複や別の木の写真が混じったため、近隣記録の比較と専門家の確認を追加し、確認済みの木に一意の番号を付与しました。従来は住民の要望中心で、声の多い地域と少ない地域の偏りがありましたが、新記録でより公平に比較でき、木の少ない街路も分かりました。ただし費用や根・枝の空間、地下の配管やケーブルの制約があり、すべての希望地にすぐ植樹できません。住民にはその理由の説明が必要でした。情報の収集は出発点であり、点検・更新・実際の判断への活用が価値を決めます。住民は毎月地域を変えて再確認し、目的と限界を理解する参加者がいることで記録が役立ち続けると期待しています。

passage.title: Keeping Track of City Trees
passage.text:
On a summer afternoon, a tree-lined street can feel quite different from a nearby road without shade. Trees also provide places for birds and insects to live. Yet city officials often have incomplete information about the trees they are responsible for. Paper records may be old, and different departments may keep separate lists. This can make it difficult to decide where care is most urgently needed.

In one city, a group of residents offered to help create a shared tree record. Volunteers walked along public streets and entered basic information into a mobile form. They recorded each tree's location, took a photograph, and noted visible signs of damage. They were not asked to judge whether a tree was safe. That decision remained the responsibility of trained specialists.

The first month produced thousands of entries, but some were unreliable. A tree near a street corner might be recorded by two teams, while a photograph taken from far away might show the wrong tree. Rather than simply count the entries, the project leader introduced a checking stage. Teams compared neighboring records, and specialists reviewed reports of possible disease. Each confirmed tree received a single identification number.

The resulting map changed how the city planned its work. Officials had previously responded mainly to requests from residents. However, some neighborhoods made many requests while others made few, even when their trees were in poor condition. The new record allowed officials to compare areas more fairly. It also revealed streets where there were very few trees at all.

The project did not mean that every neighborhood could immediately receive new trees. Planting requires money, and there must be enough space underground for roots as well as above ground for branches. In some streets, water pipes and cables limited the available space. Officials had to explain why a request could not always be accepted.

For volunteers, the main lesson was that collecting information was only the beginning. The value of the record depended on checking it, keeping it current, and using it to answer practical questions. The group now revisits a different area each month. Its members hope that a record built through public participation will remain useful because people understand both its purpose and its limits.

items.prompt: What is the main message of the final paragraph?
choices: A large number of entries always proves success.
Useful records require continued checking, updating, and practical use.
Collecting data should be completed only once.
Public participation makes professional checks unnecessary.
items.explanation: 収集に加え点検・更新・利用が必要という結論。
distractorReasons: 件数だけで判断しないと説明済み。
最終段落の三つの要件をまとめる。
毎月再確認している。
専門家の確認は継続する。
items.translation: 最終段落の主旨は何ですか。

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：25〜35語）

passage.title: Sharing School Stationery
passage.text:
Many high school students buy new notebooks, pens, and clear folders at the beginning of each school year and later realize that they have far more supplies at home than they can actually use. To put these extra items to good use, one high school placed a wooden sharing shelf beside the library entrance.

Students can leave unused stationery on the shelf whenever they tidy their desks and take items for free when they run out before class. This simple system helps families save money on school supplies and reduces the amount of usable paper and plastic thrown away.

However, some people left broken pens or torn notebooks there at first, making the shelf messy. Student volunteers now check and organize the shelf every Friday afternoon so everyone can use it comfortably.
passage.translation:
多くの高校生は新学期の初めに新しいノートやペン、クリアファイルを買うが、後になって実際に使い切れないほど多くの学用品が家にあることに気づく。こうした余剰品を有効活用するため、ある高校は図書室の入口横に木製の共有棚を設置した。
生徒は机を整理したときに未使用の文房具を棚に置き、授業前に足りなくなったときに無料で受け取れる。この手軽な仕組みにより家庭の学用品費が抑えられ、まだ使える紙やプラスチックが捨てられる量も減る。
しかし当初は壊れたペンや破れたノートを置く人もおり、棚が乱雑になった。現在は生徒ボランティアが毎週金曜日の午後に棚を点検・整理し、誰もが気持ちよく使えるようにしている。

items.model: A high school set up a shelf for sharing extra stationery, saving money and reducing waste. Because broken items were sometimes left there, student volunteers now inspect the shelf weekly.
items.translation: ある高校が余った文房具を共有する棚を設置し、出費の節約とごみ削減につなげた。壊れた物が置かれることもあったため、現在は生徒ボランティアが毎週棚を点検している。
items.explanation: 第1・2段落の「余った文房具の共有棚の設置と節約・ごみ削減の利点」と、第3段落の「破損品混入という課題と毎週のボランティア点検による解決」を30語で過不足なく統合しています。
rubric: 導入された仕組み（文房具の共有棚）と利点（節約・ごみ削減）を含めた
生じた問題（壊れた品の混入）と改善策（毎週の点検）を含めた
原文の表現をそのまま丸写しせず適切に言い換えた
本文にない自分の意見を加えず25〜35語に収めた

items.prompt:
次のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。（目安語数：50〜60語）
QUESTION: Do you think more towns should hold outdoor markets on weekends?
items.model: I think more towns should hold outdoor markets on weekends. First, residents can buy fresh vegetables directly from local farmers and learn how their food is grown. Second, weekend markets attract visitors to town centers, which supports nearby small shops and gives neighbors a lively place to talk with one another.
items.translation: 私はより多くの町が週末に屋外マーケットを開くべきだと思います。第一に、住民は地元の農家から直接新鮮な野菜を購入でき、食べ物がどのように育てられているか学べます。第二に、週末の市場は町の中心部に訪問者を呼び込み、近くの小さな店を支えるとともに近隣住民が語り合う活気ある場を生みます。
items.explanation: 賛成の立場を明確に示し、①生産者からの直接購入と食への理解、②中心市街地の小規模店舗支援と住民交流という2つの異なる視点から49〜55語帯（50語ちょうど前後）で論理的に述べています。
rubric: 週末の屋外マーケット開催への賛否を明確に述べた
生産者・消費者面と地域経済・交流面など異なる理由を2つ挙げた
接続語を用いて文と文のつながりを明確にした
50〜60語の目安に収まっている

items.explanation: 来館者の強い要望を受けて写真展の会期を2週間「延長する」なのでextendを選ぶ。

extendは「期間・範囲を延長する」。

distractorReasons: casuallyは「何気なく」。
scarcelyは「ほとんど〜ない」で安全確認の目的に合わない。
properlyは「適切に、正常に」。
narrowlyは「かろうじて」。
items.translation: 中古の自転車を購入する前、ケンジはブレーキが正常に作動するか確かめるため点検しました。

items.prompt: Residents are asked to (     ) from making loud noises on balconies after nine in the evening.
items.explanation: refrain from doingで「〜するのを控える、慎む」。夜9時以降ベランダで大きな音を立てないよう求める表現。
distractorReasons: refrain from ...で「〜を控える」。
consentは「同意」で文脈に合わない。
marginは「余白・余裕」で文脈に合わない。
shelterは「避難所」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 住民の皆様は午後9時以降、ベランダで大きな音を立てるのを控えるよう求められています。

distractorReasons: fragileは「壊れやすい」。
joint projectで「共同事業」。
hollowは「中が空洞の」。
passiveは「受動的な」。
items.translation: A：その2つの村は似た交通問題を抱えているね。 B：ええ、だから共同のバス事業を開始しました。

distractorReasons: disposableは「使い捨ての」で紙コップ側を指す。

items.prompt: Hardly anyone expected the amateur choir to win first prize, yet their performance was truly (     ).
items.explanation: 優勝を誰も予想していなかったアマチュア合唱団だが、実際の演奏は実に「見事な・注目すべき」ものだった。
distractorReasons: reluctantは「気が進まない」。
obscureは「無名の、分かりにくい」でyet以下の称賛に合わない。
artificialは「不自然な、人工的な」。
remarkableは「目覚ましい、すばらしい」。

items.prompt:

passage.text:
For shoppers with poor eyesight, choosing between dozens of similar-looking cans and boxes in a supermarket can be exhausting. Price tags on shelf edges are often printed in tiny type, and packaging designs change frequently without warning. Even regular customers may hesitate to pick up an unfamiliar brand if they cannot easily check cooking instructions or allergy warnings.

To address this problem, a regional grocery chain tested small raised QR stickers on its own-brand food packages. Unlike ordinary promotional codes that open long marketing pages, these tactile stickers can be located by touch and scanned from a wide angle. Early versions read every piece of text from top to bottom, forcing listeners to wait thirty seconds before hearing whether an item contained nuts or dairy. Unexpectedly, other customers began using the stickers too, including elderly shoppers who had left reading glasses at home and foreign residents checking unfamiliar ingredients. Designing for a specific barrier ended up creating (20).

passage.title: Why Study Rooms Added Background Sound
passage.text:
Students often assume that the best place to study is the quietest room available. Based on this idea, a municipal youth center created a strictly silent reading room on its top floor. Surprisingly, within a month, students complained that the room felt tense. In near-total silence, every cough, turning page, or chair movement sounded startlingly loud.

Acoustic specialists point out that human attention is drawn not simply to loudness, but to sudden contrasts in sound. When a room has almost no background sound, minor noises stand out sharply and break concentration. Extreme quiet had paradoxically made the room (21).

Instead of relaxing the rules and allowing loud conversations, the center divided its study floor into two zones. One zone kept the silent rule for exam takers who preferred complete stillness. The larger zone introduced soft, steady ambient sound resembling gentle rain and distant airflow. Students could also speak briefly in low voices when sharing notes. (22), a single dropped pen no longer disturbed everyone in the room.

Usage surveys three months later showed high satisfaction in both zones, with many students switching between them depending on their task. Memorizing vocabulary worked well in silence, while drafting group slides suited the moderately active room. Supporting concentration meant (23) rather than enforcing a single acoustic rule everywhere.
passage.translation: 生徒は最も静かな部屋が学習に最適だと考えがちだ。市の青少年センターも最上階に完全私語厳禁の静寂自習室を設けたが、1か月も経たないうちに「緊張感がありすぎる」と苦情が出た。ほぼ無音の空間では、咳払いやページをめくる音、椅子のきしみさえ驚くほど大きく響いたのだ。音響の専門家は、人の注意は単なる音量ではなく「急激な音の落差」に引きつけられると指摘する。背景音が皆無だとわずかな物音が際立ち集中を妨げるため、極端な静けさが逆説的にその部屋を(21)していた。センターは大声の会話を許すのではなく、フロアを2区域に分けた。一方は完全な静寂を好む受験生向けに残し、もう一方の広い区域には穏やかな雨音や空調音に近い一定の環境音を流し、ノートを見せ合う程度の小声も認めた。(22)、ペンを1本落としても部屋中の邪魔にならなくなった。3か月後の調査では両区域とも満足度が高く、暗記には静寂室、スライド作成には環境音室と課題に応じて使い分ける生徒も多かった。集中を支えるとは一律の規則を押しつけることではなく、(23)ことだったのだ。

passage.title: Guidelines for the High School Career Shadowing Day
passage.text:
From: Takashi Miura, Career Guidance Coordinator
To: Second-Year Students
Subject: Next Wednesday's workplace visits

Dear students,
Next Wednesday, November 18, all second-year students will visit local workplaces, including clinics, architectural offices, bakeries, and city departments, to observe professionals at work. Please check the bulletin board outside the guidance room today to confirm your assigned host organization and travel group.

Each group will travel directly from home to its host site rather than coming to school first. Plan to arrive ten minutes before your scheduled start time. If your train or bus is delayed, call both the school office and the contact number listed on your assignment sheet immediately.

During the visit, remember that staff members are handling real patients, clients, and deadlines. You are encouraged to ask questions during the designated Q&A session, not while employees are speaking with customers. Taking written notes in your handbook is welcome, whereas taking photographs or recording audio on smartphones is strictly prohibited to protect workplace privacy.

By the following Monday, please submit a one-page reflection sheet AND a handwritten thank-you card addressed to your host supervisor. Our office will check the cards for formal wording before mailing them together.

Best regards,
Takashi Miura
passage.translation: 差出人三浦貴志（進路指導担当）、宛先高校2年生各位、件名：来週水曜の職場見学について。11月18日（水）、2年生全員が地域の診療所・設計事務所・パン屋・市役所などを訪問し仕事を観察する。本日中に進路指導室前の掲示板で配属先と移動班を確認すること。当日は学校へ寄らず自宅から訪問先へ直行し、開始10分前に到着する計画を立てること。電車やバスが遅れた場合は直ちに学校事務室と配属票記載の連絡先の両方へ電話すること。見学中は職員が実際の患者や顧客、締切に対応していることを忘れず、質問は接客中ではなく指定の質疑応答時間に行うこと。手引きへの手書きメモは歓迎するが、職場のプライバシー保護のためスマホでの写真撮影や録音は厳禁。翌週月曜までに1ページの振り返りシートと受入担当者宛ての手書き礼状の両方を提出すること（丁寧な表現か確認した上で学校から一括郵送する）。

choices: To deliver all the cards together by school bus on Monday.
To allow staff to check the wording before the cards are mailed.
To look up the postal addresses of host workplaces for students.
To select only one card from the entire second-year class.
items.explanation: 一括郵送する前に丁寧な言葉遣いになっているか進路指導室で確認するため。
distractorReasons: スクールバスで一括配達するためではない。
発送前に教職員が文面を確認できるようにするためで本文と一致。
住所が分からないからではない。
学年で1枚だけ選ぶのではない。
items.translation: お礼状を先に進路指導室へ提出しなければならないのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Guidelines for the High School Career Shadowing Day
passage.text:
From: Takashi Miura, Career Guidance Coordinator
To: Second-Year Students
Subject: Next Wednesday's workplace visits

Dear students,
Next Wednesday, November 18, all second-year students will visit local workplaces, including clinics, architectural offices, bakeries, and city departments, to observe professionals at work. Please check the bulletin board outside the guidance room today to confirm your assigned host organization and travel group.

Each group will travel directly from home to its host site rather than coming to school first. Plan to arrive ten minutes before your scheduled start time. If your train or bus is delayed, call both the school office and the contact number listed on your assignment sheet immediately.

During the visit, remember that staff members are handling real patients, clients, and deadlines. You are encouraged to ask questions during the designated Q&A session, not while employees are speaking with customers. Taking written notes in your handbook is welcome, whereas taking photographs or recording audio on smartphones is strictly prohibited to protect workplace privacy.

By the following Monday, please submit a one-page reflection sheet AND a handwritten thank-you card addressed to your host supervisor. Our office will check the cards for formal wording before mailing them together.

Best regards,
Takashi Miura

items.prompt: According to the first paragraph, why are many small appliances thrown away?
choices: Consumers prefer heavier machines with shorter battery life.
Their motors almost always burn out within a month.
Minor worn parts cannot be replaced easily due to product design.
Electricity laws forbid keeping appliances for more than three years.

replacing a single inexpensive part requires special tools or sealed cases cannot be openedと一致。
3年以上の使用を禁じる法律はない。
items.translation: 第1段落によると、多くの小型家電が捨てられてしまうのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Why Repair Instructions Matter Before You Buy
passage.text:
When consumers shop for a toaster, a desk fan, or a cordless vacuum cleaner, they usually compare price, weight, and battery life. Rarely do they ask what will happen three years later when a switch wears out or a battery loses strength. Yet millions of small household appliances are discarded every year not because their motors have failed, but because replacing a single inexpensive part requires special tools or sealed cases cannot be opened safely.

In response, several consumer groups and regional governments have introduced "repairability scores" displayed right beside product prices in electronics stores. Instead of giving a vague environmental badge, the score rates five concrete factors from one to ten: how easily a product can be taken apart, whether spare parts are sold to the public, how many years those parts remain available, how much they cost relative to a new machine, and whether clear repair manuals can be downloaded for free.

When the scoring system first appeared, some manufacturers argued that shoppers cared only about low upfront prices and would ignore technical ratings. Early retail data suggested otherwise. Even customers who never intended to use a screwdriver themselves began choosing models with higher scores, viewing repairability as a sign of honest engineering and long-term durability.

More importantly, the visibility of low scores prompted manufacturers to change design habits before products ever reached store shelves. Engineers replaced glue with standard screws in several popular appliances and published step-by-step part diagrams online. A company might willingly tolerate a complaint buried in customer service emails, whereas a low number printed on every price tag directly affected sales.

Specialists caution that a label alone does not guarantee fewer discarded appliances. Local repair shops still need affordable parts and trained technicians, and consumers may still replace working machines when new features look appealing. Even so, making repair information visible at the moment of purchase shifts attention from how cheaply an item is made to how responsibly it can be kept in use.
passage.translation: 消費者がトースターや卓上扇風機、コードレス掃除機を買う際、価格や重さ、電池持ちは比べても、3年後にスイッチや電池が劣化したときどうなるかを尋ねることは少ない。しかし毎年何百万台もの小型家電が、モーターの寿命ではなく、安価な部品1つの交換に特殊工具が要ったり接着ケースを開けられなかったりする理由で廃棄されている。これを受け、消費者団体や自治体の一部は家電量販店の値札横に「修理しやすさスコア」を表示する制度を導入した。曖昧なエコマークではなく、分解の容易さ・一般向け交換部品の販売有無・部品供給年数・新品価格に対する部品代・無料修理説明書の公開という5項目を10段階評価する。当初メーカーの一部は消費者が初期価格の安さしか気にしないと主張したが、販売データは逆の結果を示した。自分でドライバーを握るつもりのない客でさえ、高スコアを誠実な設計と長期耐久性の証しとみなして選ぶようになったのだ。さらに低スコアが店頭で目立つことで、発売前の設計段階から接着剤を標準ネジへ改め部品図をネット公開するメーカーが増えた。メールの苦情は見過ごせても値札横の低い数字は売上に直結したからだ。もっとも、専門家は表示だけで廃棄減が保証されるわけではなく、地域の修理店への安価な部品供給や技術者育成、機能目当ての買い替え心理への向き合いも必要だと釘を刺す。それでも購入時点で修理可能性を見える化することは、いかに安く作るかから、いかに責任をもって使い続けられるかへ視点を変える力を持っている。

items.prompt: Which of the following is included in calculating the repairability score?
choices: How long replacement parts remain available and what they cost.
How many colors the appliance comes in.
How fast the store delivers the appliance to a customer's home.
Whether the product was advertised on television.
items.explanation: 分解のしやすさ、一般への部品販売、部品の供給年数、新品比の部品価格、無料マニュアルの有無の5項目で算出される。
distractorReasons: how many years those parts remain available, how much they costと一致。
カラー展開は含まれない。
配送速度は無関係。
テレビ広告の有無は無関係。
items.translation: 修理しやすさスコアの算出項目に含まれているものはどれですか。

items.prompt: What surprised some manufacturers after the scores were displayed in stores?
choices: Retail chains stopped stocking cordless vacuum cleaners without spare filters.
Shoppers began checking repairability scores alongside warranty and price tags.
Many customers asked store staff to demonstrate battery replacement at checkout.
Even shoppers who would not repair items themselves favored higher-scoring models.
items.explanation: 自分で修理するつもりのない買い物客でさえ、高スコアを誠実な設計と耐久性の証しとみて選ぶようになった。
distractorReasons: 掃除機を撤去してはいない。
価格を全く見なくなったとはない。
レジでドライバーを要求した話はない。
Even customers who never intended to use a screwdriver themselves began choosing models with higher scoresと一致。
items.translation: 店頭にスコアが表示された後、一部のメーカーを驚かせたことは何ですか。

items.prompt: How did the scoring system influence product engineers?
choices: They restricted repair manuals to certified regional service centers only.
They sealed outer plastic housings with stronger water-resistant adhesives.
They standardized battery chargers while keeping internal boards sealed.
They switched from glue to standard screws in several models and shared diagrams.
items.explanation: 店頭の低スコアが売上に影響するため、設計段階から接着剤を標準ネジへ変更し、段階的な部品図をオンライン公開した。
distractorReasons: 部品図を隠したのではなくオンライン公開した。
接着剤を増やしたのではなく標準ネジに置き換えた。
交換部品の生産をやめたのではない。
replaced glue with standard screws ... and published step-by-step part diagrams onlineと一致。
items.translation: このスコア制度は製品設計の技術者にどのような影響を与えましたか。

items.prompt: In the final paragraph, specialists point out that
choices: repair scores work well for heavy machinery but fail for home electronics.
manufacturers should set identical prices for spare parts worldwide.
labels help shift attention, though repair shops, affordable parts, and user habits also matter.
consumers should repair every appliance themselves rather than hire technicians.

最終段落の留保条件と結論を正確にまとめている。
消費者自身がすべて修理すべきとは述べていない。
items.translation: 最終段落で専門家はどのような注意を述べていますか。

passage.translation: 消費者がトースターや卓上扇風機、コードレス掃除機を買う際、価格や重さ、電池持ちは比べても、3年後にスイッチや電池が劣化したときどうなるかを尋ねることは少ない。しかし毎年何百万台もの小型家電が、モーターの寿命ではなく、安価な部品1つの交換に特殊工具が要ったり接着ケースを開けられなかったりする理由で廃棄されている。これを受け、消費者団体や自治体の一部は家電量販店の値札横に「修理しやすさスコア」を表示する制度を導入した。曖昧なエコマークではなく、分解の容易さ・一般向け交換部品の販売有無・部品供給年数・新品価格に対する部品代・無料修理説明書の公開という5項目を10段階評価する。当初メーカーの一部は消費者が初期価格の安さしか気にしないと主張したが、販売データは逆の結果を示した。自分でドライバーを握るつもりのない客でさえ、高スコアを誠実な設計と長期耐久性の証しとみなして選ぶようになったのだ。さらに低スコアが店頭で目立つことで、発売前の設計段階から接着剤を標準ネジへ改め部品図をネット公開するメーカーが増えた。メールの苦情は見過ごせても値札横の低い数字は売上に直結したからだ。もっとも、専門家は表示だけで廃棄減が保証されるわけではなく、地域の修理店への安価な部品供給や技術者育成、機能目当ての買い替え心理への向き合いも必要だと釘を刺す。それでも購入時点で修理可能性を見える化することは、いかに安く作るかから、いかに責任をもって使い続けられるかへ視点を変える力を持っている。

items.prompt: 以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。本文にない自分の意見は加えないこと。（目安語数：25〜35語）

passage.title: Digital Menus at Local Restaurants
passage.text:
Recently, many casual family restaurants have replaced traditional printed paper menus with touchscreen tablets placed at every table. Diners can view clear photographs of seasonal dishes in multiple languages, check allergy information, and send orders directly to the kitchen staff without waiting for a busy server to stop by.

This digital ordering system speeds up table service during crowded weekend lunch hours and allows restaurant managers to update daily specials or sold-out items immediately without reprinting paper pages.

However, some older customers find small buttons on bright screens confusing to navigate, and families often find it harder to compare several pages together. Consequently, thoughtful restaurants still keep printed menus available upon request.
passage.translation:
近年、多くのファミリーレストランが各テーブルに従来の紙メニューの代わりとしてタッチパネル式のタブレットを設置している。客は複数言語で季節料理の鮮明な写真やアレルギー表示を確認でき、忙しい店員を待たずに厨房スタッフへ直接注文を送れる。
このデジタル注文方式は混雑する週末の昼時の提供を速め、日替わり品や品切れ商品も紙を刷り直さず即座に更新できる。
しかし高齢客の中には明るい画面の小さなボタン操作に戸惑う人もおり、家族で複数ページを同時に見比べにくいという面もある。そのため配慮ある店舗では要望に応じて紙のメニューも常備している。

items.model: Tablet menus let restaurant customers order quickly in multiple languages and simplify menu updates. However, some diners find screens hard to use or compare, so certain restaurants still keep printed menus available.
items.translation: タブレットメニューは飲食店の客が複数言語で素早く注文できるようにし、メニュー更新も容易にする。しかし画面を使いにくい・比較しにくいと感じる客もいるため、紙のメニューを残す店もある。
items.explanation: タブレットメニューの利点（多言語・迅速な注文・即時更新）と課題（操作や一覧比較のしにくさ）、対応策（希望者向けの紙メニュー併用）を32語でバランスよく要約しています。
rubric: タブレットメニューの利点（迅速な注文・更新の容易さ等）を含めた
利用上の課題（操作の戸惑い・見比べにくさ）を含めた
店舗側の対応（紙メニューの併用）までつなげた
自分の意見を加えず25〜35語の目安に収めた

items.prompt:
次のQUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。（目安語数：50〜60語）
QUESTION: Do you think public libraries should stay open later in the evening?
items.model: I think public libraries should stay open later in the evening. First, office workers and high school students with club activities often cannot visit before early closing times, so evening hours give them fair access. Second, libraries offer a safe, quiet study space at night without requiring people to spend money at cafes.
items.translation: 私は公立図書館は夜もっと遅くまで開館すべきだと思います。第一に、会社員や部活動のある高校生は早い閉館時刻の前に行けないことが多く、夜間開館によって公平に利用できるようになります。第二に、図書館はカフェでお金を使わなくても夜に落ち着いて学べる安全で静かな場所を提供してくれます。
items.explanation: 夜間開館の延長に賛成し、First（仕事や部活で夕方まで忙しい人の利用機会確保）とSecond（費用をかけずに利用できる安全・静謐な夜間学習空間）の2つの理由を53語で明確に論じています。
rubric: 夜間開館延長に対する賛否を最初の文で明示した
利用者層・経済性など異なる2つの理由を具体的に述べた
接続表現を用いて論理的につないだ
50〜60語の目安に収まっている

items.prompt: The city council voted to (     ) the old warehouse district into a pedestrian-friendly arts quarter.

clarifyは「明確にする」で文脈に合わない。
transformは大きく変える・改修する。intoと対応。
withstandは「耐える」で文脈に合わない。

items.prompt: Because the two witnesses gave (     ) accounts of the accident, investigators checked nearby security cameras.

sortingは「選別する」で文脈に合わない。
filteringは「ろ過する」で文脈に合わない。

items.prompt: Guests with food allergies are asked to (     ) the hotel restaurant at least three days before arrival.

accommodateは「収容する」で文脈に合わない。
preserveは「保存する」で文脈に合わない。

items.prompt: Even a minor calculation error at the beginning of the experiment can (     ) the final measurements.

monitorは「監視する」で文脈に合わない。
convertは「転換する」で文脈に合わない。
distortは数値や結果をゆがめる。
items.translation: 実験の最初のわずかな計算ミスでも、最終的な測定結果をゆがめてしまうことがあります。

items.prompt: The mountain hut has limited solar power, so hikers are urged to use electricity (     ).
items.explanation: 太陽光発電の電力が限られているため、「控えめに・節約して」使うよう促されるsparingly。

abundantlyは豊富に（電力制限と逆）。

accessible toで（難しい内容が）〜にも理解できる。
marginは「余白・余裕」で文脈に合わない。
disputeは「紛争・議論」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 三浦博士の講演は、複雑な気候モデルを高校生にも分かりやすくしたことで高く評価されました。

items.prompt: The ferry service will remain suspended (     ) the harbor authorities confirm that the waves have subsided.
items.explanation: 波が収まったと港湾当局が確認する「までずっと」運休が続くのでuntil。

unlessを入れると確認しない限り運休が続くとも読めるが、時間的終点を表すuntilが最も自然かつ明確（※他選択肢との比較でも確認完了時点を示すuntilが正答）。

despiteは前置詞。
items.translation: 波が収まったと港湾当局が確認するまで、フェリーの運航は見合わせのままとなります。

take placeは開催される。

items.prompt: The coach reminded the players that consistent daily practice is no less important (     ) physical talent.
items.explanation: no less＋形容詞＋than ... で「…に劣らず重要だ」。
distractorReasons: asはas important asのときに使う。
toはinferior/superiorなどと使う。

fromは使わない。
items.translation: コーチは選手たちに、毎日の着実な練習は身体的な才能に劣らず重要だと念を押しました。

items.prompt: Several local shops agreed to (     ) the youth marathon by providing water cups and towels.
items.explanation: 紙コップやタオルを提供して青少年マラソンの「スポンサーになる・協賛する」sponsor。
distractorReasons: inspectは「点検する」で文脈に合わない。
sponsor an eventで催しに協賛・後援する。
evaluateは「評価する」で文脈に合わない。
assembleは「組み立てる」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: いくつかの地元商店が、水用のコップやタオルを提供して青少年マラソンに協賛することに同意しました。

items.prompt: Having worked in three coastal towns, Ms. Aoki has firsthand (     ) of how fishing communities adapt to storms.
items.explanation: 3つの港町で働いた経験から「直接の知識・知見」を持っているのでfirsthand knowledge of。
distractorReasons: appetiteは食欲。
shelterは避難場所。
firsthand knowledge ofで直接得た知識。
permissionは許可。
items.translation: 3つの海辺の町で働いた経験があるため、青木さんは漁村が嵐にどう適応するかについて直接の知見を持っています。

items.prompt: The committee postponed its vote because the financial figures presented at the meeting were still (     ).
items.explanation: 提示された財務数値がまだ「仮のもの・暫定的」だったため採決を延期したtentative。
distractorReasons: abundantは「豊富な」で文脈に合わない。
fragileは「壊れやすい」で文脈に合わない。
scarceは「乏しい」で文脈に合わない。
tentativeは仮の・確定していない。延期理由に合致。
items.translation: 会議で示された財務の数字がまだ暫定的なものだったため、委員会は採決を延期しました。

items.prompt: Please back up your presentation files onto an external drive in the (     ) of a network outage.
items.explanation: in the event of＋名詞で「万が一〜が起きた場合には」。
distractorReasons: on behalf ofなら〜を代表して。
in the event of a network outageで通信障害が起きた場合に備えて。
in the course ofは〜の過程で。
aspectは側面。
items.translation: 万が一ネットワーク障害が起きた場合に備え、発表用ファイルは外付けドライブにバックアップしてください。

items.prompt:
A: How does your office support new college graduates?
B: Each newcomer is paired with a mentor who helps them (     ) the workplace smoothly.
items.explanation: 新入社員が新しい職場環境にスムーズに「慣れる・なじむ」のを助けるsettle into。
distractorReasons: catch up onは遅れを取り戻す。
settle intoで新しい環境になじむ。
run out ofは使い果たす。
look down onは見下す。
items.translation:
A: あなたの職場では新卒社員をどのように支援していますか。
B: 新人それぞれに先輩がつき、職場にスムーズに馴染めるよう手助けしています。

items.prompt: The botanical garden asks visitors to stay on paved paths lest rare moss (     ) trampled.
items.explanation: lest＋主語＋(should)＋原形（be）で「〜しないように」。珍しいコケが踏みつけられないよう舗装路を歩く。
distractorReasons: 直説法現在isは標準文法のlest節に用いない。
過去形wasは不適。
lest節の仮定法現在で原形beを用いる。
will beは用いない。
items.translation: 植物園では、珍しいコケが踏み荒らされないよう舗装された歩道から出ないよう来園者に求めています。

items.prompt: The new recycling bins have color-coded lids that correspond (     ) the symbols printed on product labels.
items.explanation: correspond toで「〜に対応する・一致する」。
distractorReasons: correspond to the symbolsで記号に対応している。
atは使わない。
ofは使わない。
forは使わない。
items.translation: 新しいリサイクル回収箱には、製品ラベルに印刷された記号に対応する色分けされたふたが付いています。

items.prompt: Far from (     ) interest in print books, the town's reading festival attracted its largest crowd in ten years.
items.explanation: far from＋動名詞（losing）で「〜するどころか（それどころか逆だ）」。
distractorReasons: 過去分詞は置けない。
to不定詞は置けない。
前置詞fromの後ろに原形は置けない。
Far from losing interestで関心を失うどころか。
items.translation: 紙の本への関心を失うどころか、町の読書フェスティバルはここ10年で最大の来場者を集めました。

items.prompt: 空所(18)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。
items.explanation: 下向きフードと暖色化に加え、さらに深夜の人感センサー減光も導入したという追加説明。
distractorReasons: 逆接ではない。
さもないと、ではない。
前の文を否定していない。
In additionは「さらに・加えて」。
items.translation: 空所(18)の補充。

passage.title: Rethinking Nighttime Lighting in Parks
passage.text:
Bright streetlamps have long been installed in urban parks to help pedestrians see footpaths and feel secure after sunset. In recent years, however, ecologists and lighting engineers have pointed out an unintended side effect: unshielded white lamps scatter glare into surrounding trees and ponds, disrupting nocturnal insects, bats, and roosting birds.

When a riverside town decided to replace its aging park lamps, officials initially assumed they had to choose between human safety and wildlife protection. Turning lights off completely made evening joggers uneasy. Yet consultations with lighting specialists revealed a third approach. By fitting hoods that directed light strictly downward and shifting from harsh blue-white LEDs to warmer amber tones, the town could keep paths clearly visible while leaving tree canopies dark. (18), motion sensors dimmed secondary trails late at night when nobody was walking past.

Six months after the upgrade, insect surveys along the riverbank showed a marked recovery in moth diversity compared with brightly lit neighboring streets. Residents also responded positively; many noted that shielded lamps actually made it easier to see obstacles on the ground because (19).

The project demonstrated that environmental care does not always demand giving up public convenience. Often, the real problem lies in wasted energy—in this case, light shining into the sky where no walker needs it. Careful design allowed the park to (20).
passage.translation: 都市の公園では日没後の歩行者の安全のため明るい街灯が設置されてきましたが、近年は覆いのない白い光が周囲の樹木や池に漏れ、夜行性の昆虫やコウモリ、眠る鳥に悪影響を与えることが指摘されています。ある川沿いの町が古い街灯を更新する際、当初は「人の安全か野生生物の保護か」の二択だと思われ、完全消灯には夜間のランナーから不安が出ました。しかし照明の専門家と相談し、光を真下だけに絞るフードを付け、青白いLEDから温かみのある琥珀色に変えることで、樹冠を暗く保ちつつ歩道をはっきり照らす第3の方法が見つかりました。(18)、深夜に人が通らない小道では人感センサーで減光しました。半年後の調査では川辺のガの多様性が回復し、住民からも(19)ため地面の障害物がかえって見やすくなったと好評でした。環境配慮は必ずしも利便性の犠牲を求めるわけではなく、空へ漏れる無駄な光をなくす設計によって公園は(20)ことができました。

items.prompt: 空所(19)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。
choices: joggers were required to carry heavy lanterns
glare was no longer shining directly into pedestrians' eyes
all footpaths had been covered with white paint
trees along the river had been cut down
items.explanation: 覆い付きランプにしたことで足元が見やすくなった光学的理由。
distractorReasons: ランタン持参の義務はない。
まぶしい光が歩行者の目に直接入らなくなったため。
歩道を白く塗ったとはない。
木を切ったのでは樹冠を暗く保った話と矛盾。
items.translation: 空所(19)の補充。

items.prompt: 空所(20)に入る最も適切なものを選んでください。

double its electricity consumption every winter

passage.title: Why Recipes Sometimes Fail at High Altitude
passage.text:
Travelers staying in a mountain cabin two thousand meters above sea level are often puzzled when a familiar family recipe turns out strangely. Spaghetti takes longer to soften in boiling water, while a sponge cake that rises beautifully near the coast may puff up too fast in the oven and then collapse in the middle.

The cause is lower atmospheric pressure. At sea level, the weight of the air above pushes down on a pot of water, keeping molecules in liquid form until the temperature reaches 100 degrees Celsius. High in the mountains, thinner air exerts less pressure, so water begins boiling at around 93 degrees. Turning up the stove flame only produces more steam; it cannot make the boiling water any hotter. (21), foods cooked by boiling simply need extra minutes to finish.

Baking involves the same physics in reverse. Bubbles of steam and gas inside cake batter expand more forcefully when external air pressure is weak. Before the flour and eggs have time to set into a firm structure, the batter stretches too thin and sinks. Experienced mountain bakers compensate by reducing leavening powder slightly and raising oven temperature a little so the structure firms up sooner. (22), adding a spoonful of extra liquid prevents the batter from drying out in thin, dry mountain air.

Understanding these adjustments turns kitchen frustration into a practical science lesson. A recipe written in a coastal city assumes invisible environmental conditions. Once cooks recognize (23), they can adapt their methods confidently wherever they travel.

passage.title: Borrowing Tablets for the Field Survey
passage.text:
From: Mr. Watanabe, Geography Department
To: Fieldwork Group Leaders
Subject: Tablet checkout and offline maps for Thursday

Hello group leaders,
For Thursday's land-use survey around Kawagoe District, each group will receive one school tablet preloaded with our mapping app. Because mobile data reception can be weak near the old canal, you must download your assigned sector's offline map onto the tablet before leaving campus. Come to the geography prep room during Wednesday lunch break to check out your device and complete the download over school Wi-Fi.

During the survey, use the app to mark building types and photograph street signs, but avoid photographing private house nameplates or pedestrians' faces. Each tablet comes with a shoulder strap; whoever is carrying the device must wear the strap at all times when walking near water.

All groups must return to school by 3:45 p.m. so data can be backed up before club activities begin at 4:15 p.m. Do not delete accidental photos in the field—you might erase shared group pins by mistake. We will sort the files together back in the classroom.

Regards,
K. Watanabe
passage.translation: 地理科の渡辺先生からフィールドワーク班長への連絡。木曜の川越地区土地利用調査では地図アプリ入りの学校タブレットを各班1台貸し出す。旧運河付近は電波が弱いことがあるため、出発前に担当区画のオフライン地図をダウンロードしておく必要がある。水曜の昼休みに地理準備室へ来て端末を受け取り、校内Wi-Fiでダウンロードを済ませること。調査中は建物の種類を記録し道路標識を撮影するが、個人宅の表札や歩行者の顔は写さないこと。水辺を歩く際は落下防止のため付属のショルダーストラップを必ず着用すること。4時15分の部活動開始前にデータをバックアップするため午後3時45分までに帰校すること。共有ピンを誤消去する恐れがあるため現地で失敗写真を削除せず、帰校後に教室で一緒に整理する。

passage.title: How Libraries Handle Returned Books Behind the Scenes
passage.text:
When library patrons slip a borrowed novel through a return slot, their part of the transaction takes two seconds. Behind the wall, however, getting thousands of returned items back onto the exact shelves where the next reader can find them is a logistical challenge. Even a book placed two shelves away from its call number is effectively lost until someone spots it during a manual shelf check.

Many large public libraries have adopted radio-frequency identification, or RFID, tags—thin stickers with tiny antennas placed inside book covers—paired with conveyor belts that sort returned items into bins by floor and subject. Automation speeds up check-in and reduces repetitive strain on staff wrists. Yet technology alone has not made human judgment unnecessary.

Machines cannot easily tell whether a picture book has a torn page, whether a travel guide is missing its fold-out map, or whether rain has dampened the corners of a textbook. Staff still inspect items as they come out of the bins, setting aside damaged volumes for tape repair or drying before mildew can spread to neighboring books on the shelf. In addition, librarians watch which topics return in waves—such as gardening in April or tax guides in February—and place popular returns on front display tables rather than sending them straight to distant stacks.

Smaller branch libraries without conveyor systems rely on simple workflow rules instead. Returned books are first arranged in exact order on wheeled carts before anyone walks into the reading room, cutting shelving time in half and keeping aisles clear for visitors. New student assistants are also asked to shelve for only thirty minutes at a stretch, because fatigue sharply increases misplacement mistakes.

Whether a library uses sensor-guided belts or hand-pushed carts, accuracy depends on combining reliable routines with attentive human eyes. A catalog is useful only when the physical book is actually waiting where the screen says it is.
passage.translation: 利用者が返却ポストに本を入れるのはわずか2秒ですが、壁の向こうで何千冊もの返却本を次の読み手が見つけられる正確な棚へ戻すのは高度な物流作業です。請求記号から棚2段ずれて置かれただけでも、棚点検で見つかるまで実質的に行方不明になるからです。多くの大規模図書館では表紙裏の薄いRFIDタグとベルトコンベヤーを組み合わせ、階や分野ごとに自動仕分けして返却処理の迅速化と職員の手首の負担軽減を図っています。しかし機械だけでは人間の判断は不要になりません。絵本の破れや旅行ガイドの折り込み地図の欠落、雨によるページの湿りは機械では見抜きにくく、職員が点検して補修や乾燥を行い棚の他の本へのカビ拡大を防ぎます。また4月の園芸や2月の確定申告など季節ごとに動く本を見極め、奥の書架ではなく正面の展示台へ並べる工夫も人が担います。自動設備のない小規模分館でも、カート上で厳密に並べてから書架へ向かう手順や、疲労による配架ミスを防ぐため学生補助員の連続配架を30分に区切るルールが精度を支えています。どれほど設備が異なっても、画面上の蔵書検索が役立つのは実物の本が正しい場所に置かれていてこそなのです。

passage.title: Why Escalators Leave One Side Debate Behind
passage.text:
In many busy subway stations, commuters follow an unwritten rule on escalators: stand on one side and leave the other lane clear for people in a hurry. At first glance, this arrangement seems polite and efficient. In recent years, however, transit operators from Tokyo to London have begun asking riders to stand in both lanes and refrain from walking on moving steps.

Safety was the initial concern. Escalator steps are much taller than ordinary stairs, so a single misstep by someone carrying a bag can cause a chain of falls. Yet engineers studying station crowds found a second, surprising problem. When ninety percent of riders prefer to stand, reserving half the escalator for the few who walk leaves the walking lane mostly empty. (18), queues at the bottom grow longer during rush hour.

Field trials confirmed the math. Stations that guided commuters to stand two abreast moved roughly twenty-five percent more people per minute than stations using the stand-and-walk split. Standing evenly also reduced uneven mechanical wear on rollers and chains, because (19).

Changing habits formed over decades takes patience, of course. Clear floor footprints and calm voice reminders work better than scolding posters, helping riders understand that (20).

passage.title: Testing Acoustics with Cardboard Models
passage.text:
Before a city spends billions of yen building a concert hall, architects must be confident that a violin played softly on stage will sound warm and clear in the back balcony. Computer simulations have improved dramatically, yet sound waves bouncing off curved balconies, wooden slats, and hundreds of seats interact in ways that pure equations can still misjudge.

To catch acoustic flaws early, specialist teams often build scale models of a proposed hall—typically one-tenth the real size—out of varnished wood, dense cardboard, and miniature velvet chairs. Testing a one-tenth model requires a clever trick of physics. Because every wall and balcony is ten times smaller, engineers play test sounds at ten times their normal pitch so the wavelengths shrink in matching proportion. Tiny microphones placed where audience ears would be record how echoes decay. (21), designers can compare different ceiling angles in an afternoon without pouring a drop of concrete.

Even air inside the model needs adjustment. Ordinary room moisture absorbs ultra-high-frequency sound far faster than real hall air absorbs normal music. Teams therefore pump dry nitrogen into the sealed model or apply mathematical corrections so high notes do not vanish artificially fast. (22), miniature foam figures sit in the seats to imitate how clothed audiences soften reflections.

Once the real hall opens, musicians still fine-tune stage reflectors by ear. Even so, physical scale models provide (23) before construction cranes ever arrive.
passage.translation: 市が何十億円もかけてコンサートホールを建設する前、建築家は舞台上の繊細なバイオリンの音が後方バルコニーまで温かく明瞭に届くか確かめなければなりません。コンピュータ解析は飛躍的に進歩しましたが、曲面のバルコニーや木の格子、何百もの座席で跳ね返る音波の複雑な干渉は数式だけでは見誤ることがあります。そこで専門チームは塗装した木材や厚紙、小さなベルベット椅子で実物の10分の1ほどの縮尺模型を作ります。壁や天井が10分の1の大きさなので、波長も同じ比率で縮むよう通常の10倍の高さの試験音を鳴らし、客席の耳の位置に置いた超小型マイクで残響の減衰を測ります。(21)、コンクリートを1滴も流す前に午後の数時間で天井角度の違いを比較できます。模型内の空気にも工夫が要り、通常の湿気は超高周波音を吸収しすぎるため乾燥窒素を満たすか補正計算を行い、(22)、服を着た観客による音の吸収を再現するため小さな発泡体の人形を座席に並べます。開館後も耳での微調整は行われますが、縮尺模型はクレーンが入る前の段階で(23)を与えてくれます。

passage.title: Guidelines for the Inter-School Science Poster Exchange
passage.text:
From: Ms. Fujita, Science Committee Coordinator
To: Presenting Student Teams
Subject: Poster tube labels and presentation timing for Saturday

Dear student teams,
Twelve high schools will gather in our gymnasium this Saturday for the Prefectural Youth Science Poster Exchange. Please read these practical details carefully so setup goes smoothly in the morning.

Each team has been assigned a numbered display panel measuring 90 centimeters wide by 120 centimeters tall. Bring your printed A0 poster rolled inside a protective tube—do not fold it, as creases cast shadows under the gym spotlights and make small graphs hard to read. We will supply removable paper tape; thumbtacks and strong double-sided tape are prohibited because the panels are rented from the city hall.

To make sure every presenter also gets to view other schools' research, the two-hour session is split into odd-numbered and even-numbered rounds. Odd-numbered teams will stand by their panels for the first hour while even-numbered teams circulate, and then roles will reverse at 11:00 a.m. At least one member of your team must remain at your panel throughout your assigned hour.

Lunch boxes may be eaten in the second-floor cafeteria, not inside the gymnasium.

Best wishes,
R. Fujita
passage.translation: 理科委員会担当の藤田先生から発表生徒チームへの連絡。今週土曜、本校体育館に12校が集まり県青少年科学ポスター交流会を開く。各班には幅90センチ×高さ120センチの番号付き展示パネルが割り当てられる。A0サイズの印刷ポスターは折り目がつくとスポットライトの下で影ができ小さなグラフが読みにくくなるため、折らずに保護筒へ丸めて持参すること。市役所からの借用パネルなので画びょうや強力両面テープは禁止で、剥がせる紙テープを会場で配布する。発表者自身も他校の研究を見られるよう2時間のセッションを奇数・偶数番号で前半後半に分ける。最初の1時間は奇数番号チームがパネル前に立ち偶数チームが見学し、午前11時に交代する。担当の1時間は最低1名がパネル前に残ること。昼食は体育館内ではなく2階食堂でとること。

Odd- and even-numbered teams take turns presenting for an hour each so everyone can view other work.
items.explanation: 全員が他校の研究も見られるよう、奇数番号と偶数番号の班が1時間ずつ交代で発表と見学を行う。
distractorReasons: 舞台上で1校10分ずつの発表ではない。
教員限定の時間帯はない。
担当の1時間は最低1人が残る規則。
第3段落の運営方法と一致。
items.translation: 2時間のポスターセッションはどのように進行しますか。

passage.title: Guidelines for the Inter-School Science Poster Exchange
passage.text:
From: Ms. Fujita, Science Committee Coordinator
To: Presenting Student Teams
Subject: Poster tube labels and presentation timing for Saturday

Dear student teams,
Twelve high schools will gather in our gymnasium this Saturday for the Prefectural Youth Science Poster Exchange. Please read these practical details carefully so setup goes smoothly in the morning.

Each team has been assigned a numbered display panel measuring 90 centimeters wide by 120 centimeters tall. Bring your printed A0 poster rolled inside a protective tube—do not fold it, as creases cast shadows under the gym spotlights and make small graphs hard to read. We will supply removable paper tape; thumbtacks and strong double-sided tape are prohibited because the panels are rented from the city hall.

To make sure every presenter also gets to view other schools' research, the two-hour session is split into odd-numbered and even-numbered rounds. Odd-numbered teams will stand by their panels for the first hour while even-numbered teams circulate, and then roles will reverse at 11:00 a.m. At least one member of your team must remain at your panel throughout your assigned hour.

Lunch boxes may be eaten in the second-floor cafeteria, not inside the gymnasium.

Best wishes,
R. Fujita
passage.translation: 理科委員会担当の藤田先生から発表生徒チームへの連絡。今週土曜、本校体育館に12校が集まり県青少年科学ポスター交流会を開く。各班には幅90センチ×高さ120センチの番号付き展示パネルが割り当てられる。A0サイズの印刷ポスターは折り目がつくとスポットライトの下で影ができ小さなグラフが読みにくくなるため、折らずに保護筒へ丸めて持参すること。市役所からの借用パネルなので画びょうや強力両面テープは禁止で、剥がせる紙テープを会場で配布する。発表者自身も他校の研究を見られるよう2時間のセッションを奇数・偶数番号で前半後半に分ける。最初の1時間は奇数番号チームがパネル前に立ち偶数チームが見学し、午前11時に交代する。担当の1時間は最低1名がパネル前に残ること。昼食は体育館内ではなく2階食堂でとること。

items.prompt: What limitation of a single photograph is explained in the second paragraph?
choices: Color prints gradually lose subtle leaf contrast under bright studio lamps.
Raw macro image files are cumbersome to print in compact field handbooks.
Outdoor cameras struggle to separate pale stems from cluttered forest moss.
It shows only one specimen at one moment and cannot combine different seasonal stages naturally.
items.explanation: 写真はある一瞬の1個体（虫食い等の偶然を含む）しか写せず、春のつぼみと秋の種子のように同時に存在しない成長段階を1枚に統合しにくい。
distractorReasons: 数か月で写真が色あせるという話ではない。
海外の研究者と画像ファイルを共有できないわけではない。
緑色の識別不能ではなく1個体の一時点しか写せず季節をまたぐ器官を自然に統合できない点。
第2段落の2つの理由と一致。
items.translation: 第2段落で説明されている1枚の写真の限界は何ですか。

passage.title: Why Botanical Illustrators Still Draw by Hand
passage.text:
Modern digital cameras can capture every vein on a flower petal in a fraction of a second, complete with accurate color and microscopic sharpness. Given such tools, newcomers to botanical science are often surprised to learn that major herbaria and natural history museums still commission trained artists to draw newly described plant species in pen and ink.

A photograph records a single individual plant at one exact moment—under specific lighting, with whatever insect bite, wilted leaf, or overlapping stem happens to be present that afternoon. Taxonomists naming a species, however, need an image that shows the defining traits shared across healthy specimens, free from distracting accidents. Even more importantly, a single botanical plate can combine stages of life that never appear on one plant simultaneously: spring buds, summer blossoms, autumn seed capsules, and underground root structures.

Depth of field poses another challenge under high magnification. When a camera zooms in on a tiny three-millimeter flower, the front stamens may look razor-sharp while structures two millimeters farther back blur into haze. An illustrator examining the specimen through a dissecting microscope adjusts focus continuously and draws every layer with equal clarity, using subtle line weights so viewers immediately grasp which parts sit in front.

Far from working by artistic whim, botanical illustrators collaborate closely with botanists. Before inking a final sheet, the artist prepares pencil layouts measured with calipers, and the researcher checks the angle of tiny hairs or the exact number of scales on a stem. Sometimes the act of drawing uncovers diagnostic details that the scientist had overlooked during initial notes.

Photography and illustration are therefore partners rather than rivals in plant science. Photos document habitat and living color in the field, while ink drawings distill complex three-dimensional anatomy into clear, lasting visual explanations.

items.prompt: How does a botanical illustrator overcome the focus problem seen in high-magnification photography?
choices: By tracing outlines from nineteenth-century lithographs stored in archives.
By selecting only large mature specimens whose parts are visible without lenses.
By adjusting microscope focus across layers and drawing all parts clearly with varied line weights.
By pressing the specimen flat between glass plates before sketching.
items.explanation: 解剖顕微鏡のピントを少しずつ動かして観察し、線の太さを使い分けながら手前から奥まで全ての層を鮮明に描く。
distractorReasons: 19世紀の古い石版画を書き写すのではない。
大型標本だけを選んで描くわけではない。
第3段落の記述と一致。
ガラス板に挟んで平らに潰してから描くのではない。
items.translation: 植物画家は高倍率写真で見られるピントの問題をどう克服しますか。

items.prompt: Why do botanists and illustrators work closely together during the pencil-sketch stage?
choices: To ensure measurements and tiny structural details are scientifically accurate.
To choose natural background shading for botanical museum exhibition posters.
To match fresh wildflower colors against pressed herbarium reference sheets.
To adapt technical Latin descriptions for introductory university textbooks.
items.explanation: ノギスで測った下絵の段階で、微細な毛の角度や茎の鱗片の数など分類上の特徴が科学的に正確か確認し合うため。
distractorReasons: 第4段落の共同作業の内容と一致。
ミュージアムショップ用ポスターの背景色を選ぶためではない。
種子袋と写真を比べるためではない。
子ども向けに葉の形を単純化するためではない。
items.translation: 鉛筆下絵の段階で植物学者と画家が緊密に協力するのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: What sometimes happens while an illustrator is carefully drawing a specimen?
choices: Blurry field photographs can be discarded once ink plates are finished.
The artist notices distinguishing features that the researcher initially missed.
Pressed petals regain their original shape under humid studio lighting.
Delicate stamens curl inward before caliper measurements are completed.
items.explanation: Sometimes the act of drawing uncovers diagnostic details that the scientist had overlookedとある。
distractorReasons: 写真は生きた色や環境記録として併用される。
研究者が最初のメモで見落としていた識別上の特徴が見つかることがある。
一晩で別種に変わることはない。
計測前に標本が乾いてダメになるという話ではない。
items.translation: 画家が標本を丁寧に描いている最中に時々起きることは何ですか。

items.prompt: How does the author view the relationship between photography and hand illustration in botany?
choices: Photography works well in labs but is unreliable outdoors.
Each method has distinct strengths that complement the other.
Both methods have been replaced by verbal descriptions alone.
Hand illustration will make field cameras obsolete within five years.
items.explanation: 現地での色や環境を記録する写真と、複雑な立体構造を明快に抽出する線画はライバルではなく互いに補い合うパートナーだとしている。
distractorReasons: 屋外で写真が使えないとは述べていない（むしろ生きた色を捉える）。
最終段落のpartners rather than rivalsと一致。
文章だけに置き換わったとはない。
カメラが廃れるとは言っていない。
items.translation: 筆者は植物学における写真と手描き図の関係をどう捉えていますか。

items.prompt: The coastal road will be widened next spring to (     ) heavy weekend traffic near the ferry terminal.
items.explanation: 週末の激しい交通渋滞を「緩和する・和らげる」ために道路を拡幅するのでrelieve。
distractorReasons: convertは「転換する」で文脈に合わない。
relieve heavy trafficで渋滞を緩和する。
eliminateは「取り除く」で文脈に合わない。
monitorは「監視する」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: フェリー乗り場近くの週末の激しい渋滞を緩和するため、来春その海岸道路が拡幅されます。

items.prompt: Even minor cracks in a ceramic teapot can cause it to leak once boiling water makes the clay (     ).
items.explanation: 熱湯によって粘土がわずかに「膨張する」ことで小さなひびから水漏れするexpand。
distractorReasons: generateは「生み出す」で文脈に合わない。
inspectは「点検する」で文脈に合わない。
postponeは「延期する」で文脈に合わない。
expandは熱などで膨張する・広がる。
items.translation: 陶器の急須のわずかなひびでも、熱湯で粘土が膨張すると水漏れの原因になることがあります。

items.prompt: The wooden annex lacks central heating. As a result, it is used only on a (     ) basis during mild spring and autumn weeks.
items.explanation: 穏やかな春と秋の時期にだけ「季節限定で」使われるon a seasonal basis。
distractorReasons: fragileは「壊れやすい」で文脈に合わない。
seasonalは季節的な・季節限定の。
thoroughは「徹底的な」で文脈に合わない。
neutralは「中立の」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: その木造の別棟には中央暖房がないため、穏やかな春と秋の週に限って季節的に使われています。

items.prompt: The town's disaster map is updated every two years in (     ) with neighborhood fire captains.
items.explanation: in consultation with ... で「…と協議のうえ・相談しながら」。
distractorReasons: in consultation withで〜と相談して。
warrantyは「保証」で文脈に合わない。
priorityは「優先事項」で文脈に合わない。
shortageは「不足」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 町の防災マップは、地区の消防団長たちと協議しながら2年ごとに更新されています。

items.prompt: At first the two painters worked in very different styles, yet over time they had a strong mutual (     ) on each other.

passage.title: Why Supermarkets Sell "Weather-Marked" Fruit
passage.text:
Shoppers choosing apples or pears in a supermarket often equate smooth, spotless skin with good flavor. As a result, fruit whose skin was lightly scratched by wind-blown twigs or summer hail is frequently rejected by retail buyers, even when the flesh underneath is just as crisp and sweet as top-grade produce.

After an early autumn typhoon scarred nearly forty percent of one orchard town's apple crop, local cooperatives tried a different approach rather than selling the fruit cheaply for juice alone. They packed the apples in clear bags with a small illustrated card explaining how wind marks form on branches and assuring buyers that the inside was unaffected. Supermarkets priced these "weather-marked" bags twenty percent lower than gift-grade fruit. (18), families looking for everyday snacks bought out the first shipment within days.

Follow-up surveys showed an interesting shift in customer attitudes. Shoppers who tasted the discounted apples realized that minor surface marks had no bearing on sweetness or storage life. (19), orchards earned nearly double what juice factories would have paid, helping farmers cover pruning and repair costs after the storm.

Cosmetic standards still matter for formal seasonal gifts, of course. Yet giving honest context at the shelf proved that (20).
passage.translation: スーパーでリンゴや梨を選ぶ買い物客は、傷ひとつない滑らかな皮をおいしさの証と考えがちです。そのため風に揺れた小枝や夏のひょうで皮に薄い擦り傷がついた果物は、果肉の歯ごたえや甘みが一級品と変わらなくても仕入れ段階で敬遠されてきました。ある果樹産地の町で初秋の台風によりリンゴの約4割に傷がついた際、地元農協はジュース原料として安値で手放す代わりに別の方法を試みました。枝で風傷ができる仕組みと中身に問題がないことを絵入りカードで添え、贈答・特秀品より2割安く販売したのです。(18)、日常のおやつを探していた家庭が数日で初回入荷分を買い切りました。追跡調査では客の意識にも変化が見られ、表面の小さな傷は甘さや日持ちに関係ないと実感されました。(19)、農家はジュース工場向けのほぼ2倍の収入を得て嵐の後の剪定や補修費を賄えました。贈答用の見た目基準は残るものの、売り場で正直な背景を伝えたことは(20)と証明しました。

passage.title: Keeping Bus Timetables Readable for Everyone
passage.text:
Public transit agencies pack an impressive amount of data onto a single bus-stop sign: weekday runs, Saturday schedules, holiday exceptions, fare zones, and route branches. For regular commuters who ride the same 7:42 a.m. bus every day, dense columns of tiny numbers soon become familiar. For an occasional rider, an older resident with declining eyesight, or a visitor standing in the rain, however, reading that grid can feel like solving a puzzle.

When a coastal city redesigned its three hundred bus-stop poles, designers began by watching people actually use the signs. Many riders traced rows with a finger because closely spaced lines caused their eyes to jump from the 8:00 row to the 9:00 row. Simply increasing font size was not enough on narrow poles, so the team removed repeated minute labels, grouped departures by morning, midday, and evening bands, and added subtle gray shading to every second row. (21), misreading errors in user tests dropped by more than half.

Equally helpful was replacing text-heavy footnotes—such as "Buses marked with a triangle bypass Harbor Hospital on Sundays"—with a small diagram showing the two route branches visually. Riders grasped where each numbered bus went in seconds rather than hunting for tiny symbols at the bottom of the board. (22), high-contrast black ink on matte yellow-white panels reduced glare under both midday sun and streetlamps.

Digital arrival apps are convenient, yet batteries die and tourists may lack data plans. Treating the humble bus-stop sign as serious information design ensures that (23).
passage.translation: 路線バスの停留所標識には平日・土曜・祝日の時刻や運賃区間、系統の分岐など膨大な情報が詰め込まれています。毎朝同じ7時42分発に乗る常連客には小さな数字の列もじきに見慣れますが、たまに乗る人や視力が落ちてきた高齢者、雨の中で立つ旅行者にはパズルのように感じられます。ある海辺の市が300基のバス停標識を刷新した際、デザイナーが利用者を観察すると、行間が狭いため指でなぞらないと8時台から9時台へ目線がずれる人が多くいました。細い柱では単に文字を大きくするだけでは収まらないため、重複表記を整理して朝・昼・夕の帯に分け、1行おきに薄いグレーの網掛けを入れました。(21)、利用者テストでの読み間違いは半分以下に減りました。また「三角印は日曜に港病院を通過」といった細かい注記を小さな分岐図に置き換えたことで、数秒で行き先が分かるようになりました。(22)、つや消しの淡黄色パネルに高コントラストの黒文字を使ったことで日中の日差しでも夜間の街灯下でも反射が抑えられました。素朴なバス停標識を真剣に設計することは(23)を確実にします。
