passage.title: Distinguishing "Social Jetlag" from Sleep Debt
passage.text:
Most high schoolers and office workers know the groggy feeling of short weekday sleep, and many try to make up for six-hour weeknights by sleeping until eleven a.m. on Saturdays and Sundays. Catching extra rest certainly feels refreshing on Sunday afternoon. Yet chronobiologists—researchers who study the body's twenty-four-hour circadian clocks—have found that swinging wildly between early weekday alarms and late weekend sleep-ins creates a hidden disruption they call "social jetlag."

Every organ in the human body, from liver enzymes and gut bacteria to blood-pressure hormones, runs on daily timing cues coordinated by a master clock in the brain's hypothalamus. That master clock calibrates itself primarily by when bright morning light first hits the retina. Stay up until two a.m. on Friday and Saturday and draw the curtains until noon, and your biological clock shifts roughly two to three hours westward—essentially flying your internal organs from Tokyo to Bangkok for the weekend.

When Monday's six-thirty alarm rings, forcing yourself out of bed does not snap those internal clocks back into place immediately; the pancreas and digestive tract may still expect midnight rest while you eat breakfast. Epidemiological studies tracking thousands of adults and teens show that even among people who average seven and a half hours of sleep per night across the week, a weekend midpoint shift of two hours or more correlates with foggier Monday memory, mood dips, and poorer blood-sugar regulation.

Sleep clinicians do not advise exhausted students to forfeit rest altogether, of course. Rather than sleeping until noon, they recommend anchoring wake-up times within sixty to ninety minutes of weekday schedules, stepping into outdoor daylight right after rising, and taking a brief twenty-minute early-afternoon nap if needed.

Consistent rhythm, it turns out, nourishes the brain nearly as much as total hours on the pillow.
passage.translation: 多くの高校生や会社員は平日の睡眠不足によるだるさを経験しており、平日の6時間睡眠を埋め合わせようと土日に昼の11時まで寝だめをしがちです。日曜の午後はすっきりした気分になるものの、体内時計を研究する時間生物学者たちは、平日の早起きと週末の遅起きを大きく行き来することが「ソーシャル・ジェットラグ（社会的時差ぼけ）」という見えない不調を生むことを突き止めました。肝臓の酵素から血圧ホルモンまで全身の臓器は脳の視床下部にある親時計に統率されており、その時計は朝の明るい光が目に入る時刻でリセットされます。金・土曜に深夜2時まで起きて昼までカーテンを閉めていると、体内時計は2〜3時間西へずれ、週末だけ東京からバンコクへ飛行機で移動したのと同じ状態になります。月曜朝6時半の目覚ましで無理に起きても内臓の時計はすぐには戻らず、週平均の睡眠時間が7時間半足りている人でも週末の睡眠中央時刻が2時間以上ずれると月曜の記憶力低下や気分の落ち込み、血糖調整の乱れと関連することが分かっています。専門家は昼まで寝続ける代わりに、起床時刻のずれを平日の60〜90分以内に保ち朝の屋外光を浴び、必要なら昼過ぎに20分の短い昼寝をとることを勧めています。睡眠は合計時間だけでなく「一定のリズム」が脳を支えているのです。

items.prompt: What primary signal resets the master biological clock in the human brain each day?
choices: When bright morning light first reaches the eyes.
The sound of a smartphone alarm ringtone.
Eating a heavy dinner at ten p.m.
Checking a wall calendar on Monday morning.
items.explanation: That master clock calibrates itself primarily by when bright morning light first hits the retina.とある。
distractorReasons: 朝の明るい光が網膜に届くタイミング。
アラーム音ではない。
夜10時の重い夕食ではない。
カレンダーを見ることではない。
items.translation: 人間の脳にある親時計を毎日リセットする主な合図は何ですか。

passage.title: Distinguishing "Social Jetlag" from Sleep Debt
passage.text:
Most high schoolers and office workers know the groggy feeling of short weekday sleep, and many try to make up for six-hour weeknights by sleeping until eleven a.m. on Saturdays and Sundays. Catching extra rest certainly feels refreshing on Sunday afternoon. Yet chronobiologists—researchers who study the body's twenty-four-hour circadian clocks—have found that swinging wildly between early weekday alarms and late weekend sleep-ins creates a hidden disruption they call "social jetlag."

Every organ in the human body, from liver enzymes and gut bacteria to blood-pressure hormones, runs on daily timing cues coordinated by a master clock in the brain's hypothalamus. That master clock calibrates itself primarily by when bright morning light first hits the retina. Stay up until two a.m. on Friday and Saturday and draw the curtains until noon, and your biological clock shifts roughly two to three hours westward—essentially flying your internal organs from Tokyo to Bangkok for the weekend.

When Monday's six-thirty alarm rings, forcing yourself out of bed does not snap those internal clocks back into place immediately; the pancreas and digestive tract may still expect midnight rest while you eat breakfast. Epidemiological studies tracking thousands of adults and teens show that even among people who average seven and a half hours of sleep per night across the week, a weekend midpoint shift of two hours or more correlates with foggier Monday memory, mood dips, and poorer blood-sugar regulation.

Sleep clinicians do not advise exhausted students to forfeit rest altogether, of course. Rather than sleeping until noon, they recommend anchoring wake-up times within sixty to ninety minutes of weekday schedules, stepping into outdoor daylight right after rising, and taking a brief twenty-minute early-afternoon nap if needed.

Consistent rhythm, it turns out, nourishes the brain nearly as much as total hours on the pillow.
passage.translation: 多くの高校生や会社員は平日の睡眠不足によるだるさを経験しており、平日の6時間睡眠を埋め合わせようと土日に昼の11時まで寝だめをしがちです。日曜の午後はすっきりした気分になるものの、体内時計を研究する時間生物学者たちは、平日の早起きと週末の遅起きを大きく行き来することが「ソーシャル・ジェットラグ（社会的時差ぼけ）」という見えない不調を生むことを突き止めました。肝臓の酵素から血圧ホルモンまで全身の臓器は脳の視床下部にある親時計に統率されており、その時計は朝の明るい光が目に入る時刻でリセットされます。金・土曜に深夜2時まで起きて昼までカーテンを閉めていると、体内時計は2〜3時間西へずれ、週末だけ東京からバンコクへ飛行機で移動したのと同じ状態になります。月曜朝6時半の目覚ましで無理に起きても内臓の時計はすぐには戻らず、週平均の睡眠時間が7時間半足りている人でも週末の睡眠中央時刻が2時間以上ずれると月曜の記憶力低下や気分の落ち込み、血糖調整の乱れと関連することが分かっています。専門家は昼まで寝続ける代わりに、起床時刻のずれを平日の60〜90分以内に保ち朝の屋外光を浴び、必要なら昼過ぎに20分の短い昼寝をとることを勧めています。睡眠は合計時間だけでなく「一定のリズム」が脳を支えているのです。

items.prompt: The study noted even among people who averaged 7.5 hours of sleep across the week that
choices: students averaging 7.5 hours avoided Monday grogginess provided they napped on Sunday afternoon.
participants with shifting weekend schedules consumed fewer snacks after evening study sessions.
those whose weekend sleep shifted by two or more hours still showed Monday memory fog and poorer metabolic control.
catching up on sleep until late Sunday morning restored alertness by Tuesday morning classes.
items.explanation: even among people who average seven and a half hours ... a weekend midpoint shift of two hours or more correlates with foggier Monday memory, mood dips, and poorer blood-sugar regulationとある。
distractorReasons: 週平均7.5時間寝ていても週末に2時間以上ずれると月曜の不調が見られた。
午前の授業中の消費カロリーが増えたという結果ではない。
週平均の睡眠時間が足りていても、週末のずれが2時間以上あると月曜の認知低下や血糖調整の乱れが見られた。
日曜昼までの寝だめで月曜の反応速度が完全回復したとは逆。
items.translation: 週平均で7時間半眠っている人たちの間でも、どのような注目すべき調査結果が出ましたか。

items.prompt: What weekend strategy do sleep clinicians recommend instead of sleeping until noon?
choices: Rest in a darkened bedroom on Sunday morning and take a ninety-minute nap right before dinner.
Keep wake-up times within 60–90 minutes of weekdays, get morning outdoor light, and use a short early-afternoon nap if tired.
Wake at weekday times on Saturday morning and do vigorous outdoor exercise late on Sunday night.
Go to bed two hours early on Friday evening so weekend wake-up times stay close to weekday routines.
items.explanation: anchoring wake-up times within sixty to ninety minutes of weekday schedules, stepping into outdoor daylight right after rising, and taking a brief twenty-minute early-afternoon napとある。
distractorReasons: 朝の光を避けて夕方に長時間昼寝するのはどちらも逆効果。
第4段落の具体的な3つの助言と完全一致。
平日より2時間早起きする指示ではない。
土曜に朝寝坊して日曜だけ3時間早く寝ようとしても体内時計はすぐ戻らない。
items.translation: 昼まで寝だめする代わりに、睡眠の専門家はどのような週末の過ごし方を勧めていますか。

items.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the passage's central conclusion?
choices: Shifting weekend wake-up schedules affects mood briefly without altering glucose metabolism.
Maintaining a steady daily sleep-wake rhythm matters nearly as much for health and alertness as total sleep duration.
High school students function well on five hours of sleep if they wake at the same hour daily.
International airline passengers recover from jetlag much faster than night-shift workers do.
items.explanation: Consistent rhythm, it turns out, nourishes the brain nearly as much as total hours on the pillow.とある。
distractorReasons: 気分だけでなくインスリン感受性など代謝や体内時計の協調にも影響する。
最終文の結論と完全一致。
睡眠時間の総量が短くてよいとは述べていない（総時間とリズム安定の両方が重要）。
海外旅行の時差ボケと交代勤務の回復速度比較が主題ではない。
items.translation: 本文の中心的な結論を最もよく要約しているのはどれですか。

items.prompt:
A: River ice breaks up unpredictably in late March.
B: Yes, so kayak rentals remain (     ) until harbor patrol boats clear the channel.
items.explanation: 3月下旬は川氷が予測しがたく割れるため、巡視艇が水路の安全を確認するまでカヤック貸出は「一時停止された」状態のままであるremain suspended。
distractorReasons: suspend service/rentalsで貸出や業務を一時中止する。
allocatedは「割り当てられた」で文脈に合わない。
depletedは「枯渇した」で文脈に合わない。
verifiedは「検証された」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: A：3月下旬は川の氷がいつ割れるか予測できないね。 B：ええ、だから港の巡視艇が水路の安全を確認するまでカヤックの貸出は休止されています。

items.prompt:
A: The two violin bows weighed almost the same.
B: Even so, the concertmaster noticed an (     ) improvement in bounce and tone with the older stick.
items.explanation: 重さはほぼ同じだったにもかかわらず、コンサートマスターは古い弓のほうが跳ね返りや音色に「非常に大きな・計り知れない」向上があることに気づいたimmense improvement。
distractorReasons: scarceは「乏しい」で文脈に合わない。
ambiguousは「曖昧な」で文脈に合わない。
immense improvementで非常に大きな改善。Althoughの対比と合致。
vibrantは「活気のある」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: A：その2本のバイオリンの弓は重さがほぼ同じでしたね。 B：それでも、コンサートマスターは古い弓のほうが弾みと音色が格段に優れていることに気づきました。

items.prompt: To stop coastal dunes from blowing onto the railway tracks, volunteers spent Saturday morning (     ) native beach grass along the ridge.
items.explanation: 海岸砂丘の砂が線路へ吹き込むのを防ぐため、砂丘の尾根に沿って在来の海浜植物の苗を「移植する・植え替える」作業を行ったtransplanting。
distractorReasons: curbingは「抑制する」で文脈に合わない。
disruptingは「混乱させる」で文脈に合わない。
transplant seedlings/grassで植物を移植する。
bolsteringは「強化する」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 海岸の砂丘から線路へ砂が吹き込むのを防ぐため、ボランティアは土曜の午前中をかけて砂丘の背に在来の海浜草を植えつけました。

items.prompt: Before returning borrowed brass instruments at graduation, band seniors have every valve and slide professionally (     ).
items.explanation: 卒業時に借用していた金管楽器を返却する前に、すべてのピストンと抜き差し管を専門職人に「整備・点検手入れしてもらう」have ... serviced。
distractorReasons: divertedは「迂回させられた」で文脈に合わない。
concealedは「隠された」で文脈に合わない。
endorsedは「承認された」で文脈に合わない。
have an instrument/car servicedで専門家に整備・メンテナンスしてもらう。
items.translation: 卒業時に借りていた金管楽器を返却する前に、吹奏楽部の3年生はすべてのバルブとスライドを専門店で整備してもらいます。

items.prompt: Pediatricians are increasingly (     ) about energy drinks marketed to middle schoolers because caffeine disrupts adolescent deep sleep.
items.explanation: カフェインが思春期の深い睡眠を妨げるため、中学生向けエナジードリンクに対して小児科医たちはますます「声高に意見を述べる・積極的に警鐘を鳴らす」ようになっているvocal about ...。
distractorReasons: feasibleは「実現可能な」で文脈に合わない。
durableは「丈夫な」で文脈に合わない。
tediousは「単調で退屈な」で文脈に合わない。
be vocal about ... で…について率直・積極的に声を上げる。
items.translation: カフェインが十代の深い睡眠を妨げるため、中学生向けに宣伝されるエナジードリンクに対して小児科医たちはますます強く警鐘を鳴らすようになっています。

items.prompt: Installing rubber pads beneath the rooftop heat pump brought welcome (     ) to tenants sleeping on the top floor.
items.explanation: 屋上ヒートポンプの下に防振ゴムパッドを敷いたことで、最上階で眠る入居者に喜ばしい「静けさ・平穏」がもたらされたquietude。
distractorReasons: resentmentは憤慨。
quietudeは静寂・穏やかさ。rooftop heat pumpの防振対策と合致。
reluctanceは気乗りしないこと。
quarrelは口論。
items.translation: 屋上のヒートポンプの下に防振ゴムパッドを設置したことで、最上階で眠る入居者たちにありがたい静けさが戻りました。

items.prompt: To keep fragile soy-milk skin intact while lifting it from hot vats, artisans slide flat bamboo skewers underneath lest it (     ).
items.explanation: 熱い釜から薄い湯葉をすくい上げる際、「破れる」ことがないよう平たい竹串を下へ滑り込ませるlest it tear。
distractorReasons: diminishは「減少させる」で文脈に合わない。
lest S + (should) 原形で「〜しないように」。tearは破れる。
facilitateは「促進する」で文脈に合わない。
surpassは「上回る」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 熱い釜から繊細な湯葉を引き上げる際、職人たちは破れないように平たい竹串をそっと下へ差し込みます。

items.prompt:
A: I heard salt spray corroded the seaside traffic signal box.
B: That's right. Afterward, technicians (     ) the rusted steel cabinet with fiberglass housing.
items.explanation: 潮風で海沿いの信号制御箱が腐食した際、技術者は錆びた鋼鉄製キャビネットをガラス繊維強化樹脂製の筐体に「取り替えた」replaced A with B。
distractorReasons: replace A with BでAをBに取り替える。
compiledは「集計された」で文脈に合わない。
dispersedは「分散した」で文脈に合わない。
obscuredは「遮られた」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 潮風で海沿いの信号機の制御箱が腐食したため、技術者は錆びた鋼鉄製の箱をグラスファイバー製の容器に取り替えました。

items.prompt: The twin pottery kilns use identical clay and pine firewood. However, glaze colors emerge (     ) warmer in the chamber closer to the chimney.
items.explanation: 同じ粘土と赤松薪を使っていても、煙突に近い焼成室のほうが釉薬の色合いが「目立って・はっきりと」温かみのある色に焼き上がるnoticeably warmer。
distractorReasons: abruptlyは「突然に」で文脈に合わない。
noticeably warmerで目に見えて温かみがある。Althoughとの対比に自然。
explicitlyは「明示的に」で文脈に合わない。
virtuallyは「事実上」で文脈に合わない。

passage.title: Why Bridges Have Finger-Shaped Metal Joints
passage.text:
Drive or cycle across a long river bridge, and you will occasionally hear a rhythmic double thump beneath your tires while passing over a row of interlocking steel "fingers" set flush into the asphalt. Commuters rarely give those toothed metal plates a second glance, yet without expansion joints spaced carefully along the deck, a steel or concrete bridge would literally tear itself apart within a single year of seasonal weather.

Solid as bridge girders appear, every span behaves like a giant thermometer. On a freezing January midnight and a blazing August afternoon, a three-hundred-meter steel bridge can shrink and lengthen by more than fifteen centimeters as metal atoms vibrate faster in the heat. If engineers bolted both ends rigidly into concrete abutments, summer expansion would buckle the roadway upward, while winter contraction would crack supporting piers. (18), leaving a plain open slot wide enough to absorb fifteen centimeters of movement would create a dangerous trench capable of trapping bicycle wheels and jarring car suspensions.

Interlocking finger joints solve both problems elegantly. Two heavy steel plates cast with long tapered teeth are anchored to opposite deck sections so their fingers slide smoothly past one another as the bridge breathes in and out. Even when the gap opens widest in midwinter, vehicle tires roll continuously across overlapping steel teeth rather than dropping into a void. (19), rubber drainage troughs slung underneath catch salty slush and grit before runoff can rust structural bearings below.

Next time tires click softly over a bridge deck, that brief sound marks hardware that (20).
passage.translation: 長い川の橋を車や自転車で渡ると、アスファルトと同じ高さに埋め込まれた鋼鉄の「指」が噛み合う継ぎ目の上でタイヤがリズミカルにトン、トンと鳴ることがあります。普段は気にも留めない金属板ですが、この伸縮装置がなければ鋼橋やコンクリート橋は1年の寒暖差だけで自壊してしまいます。長さ300メートルの鋼橋は真冬の深夜と真夏の午後とで15センチ以上も伸縮するため、両端を橋台に完全固定すれば夏は路面が盛り上がり冬は橋脚にひびが入ります。(18)、15センチの隙間をただ開けておけば自転車の車輪が落ちる危険な溝になってしまいます。噛み合わせ式のフィンガージョイントは両側の桁に細長い鋼の歯を互い違いに配置し、冬に最も隙間が開いてもタイヤが途切れず歯の上を渡れるようにしています。(19)、下に吊られたゴム製の排水樋が融雪塩を含んだ泥水を受け止め、下の支承が錆びるのを防ぎます。タイヤの軽い通過音は、(20)装置が働いている証しなのです。

passage.title: How Rooftop Solar Panels Pair Well with Meadows
passage.text:
For years, architects designing flat commercial roofs treated green roofs and solar panels as competing choices: an owner could either lay trays of drought-hardy sedum plants to absorb stormwater or bolt down racks of photovoltaic modules to generate clean electricity. Across Germany, Switzerland, and Japan, however, building scientists are increasingly combining both systems into "biosolar" rooftops—discovering that plants and silicon cells actually help each other perform better.

A bare black waterproof membrane on a sunny July roof can easily bake at sixty-five degrees Celsius. Counterintuitively, solar panels lose electrical efficiency once their cells heat much above twenty-five degrees, dropping output just when afternoon air conditioners demand maximum power. When low-growing native wildflowers and mosses carpet the soil beneath raised panel frames, moisture evaporating gently from leaves cools the surrounding air by several degrees. (21), panels hovering overhead stay cooler and generate up to five percent more summer electricity than identical arrays mounted over bare gravel or tar.

The partnership works just as generously in reverse. Unshaded rooftop gardens often scorch into uniform mats of tough succulents, leaving little variety for urban insects. Angled solar frames create a patchwork of sunny strips, dappled shade, and rain-drip lines across the soil bed. (22), dozens of wildflower species bloom in staggered waves from April through October, feeding solitary bees and hoverflies high above busy streets.

Provided roof beams are engineered for wet soil weight, pairing greenery with solar arrays turns idle rooftops into (23).
passage.translation: 長年、商業ビルの陸屋根設計では「屋上緑化」と「太陽光パネル」は二者択一だと考えられてきました。しかし現在、ドイツやスイス、日本では両者を組み合わせる「バイオソーラー（緑化一体型太陽光）」屋上が広がり、植物と太陽電池が互いの性能を高め合うことが分かっています。真夏の黒い防水シート上は65度にも達しますが、太陽電池は25度を大きく超えると発電効率が落ちる弱点があります。架台の下に背の低い在来草花やコケを植えると葉の蒸散で周囲の空気が数度冷やされ、(21)、裸の砂利や防水層の上より夏の発電量が最大5％向上します。逆方向の恩恵も大きく、日陰のない屋上緑化は乾燥に強い多肉植物ばかりになりがちですが、傾斜したパネルが日向と木漏れ日、雨だれの変化をつくるため、(22)、春から秋まで多様な野花が咲き継ぎハチやヒラタアブを養います。湿った土の荷重に耐える構造設計さえ整えば、この組み合わせは屋上を(23)へと変えてくれます。

items.prompt: How does outdoor raku firing differ from an ordinary electric kiln firing?
choices: Low-fire clay pots are baked slowly under buried charcoal for forty-eight hours.
Red-hot pieces are pulled straight from the kiln with tongs and placed into dry sawdust.
Glazed bowls cool overnight inside the sealed kiln before touching outside air.
Biscuit-fired pieces are dipped in cold river water right before entering the flame.
items.explanation: raku pieces are lifted red-hot from the gas kiln at nine hundred degrees with long iron tongs and placed straight into metal bins filled with dry sawdustとある。
distractorReasons: 48時間の炭火蒸し焼きではない。
900度で赤熱した器を鉄ばさみで取り出し、おがくずの缶へ直接入れる。
窯の中で一晩かけて自然冷却するのは通常の電気窯焼成。
焼成直前に冷水に浸すのではない。
items.translation: 屋外の楽焼焼成は通常の電気窯焼成とどう異なりますか。

passage.title: Preparing Pottery Pieces for the Raku Firing Day
passage.text:
From: Ceramics Club Advisor, Makoto Hori
To: All Registered Raku Workshop Potters
Subject: Clay choice and dress rules for Saturday's outdoor raku firing

Hello everyone,
Our outdoor raku firing behind the art studio is set for this Saturday from 9:30 a.m. Unlike ordinary electric kiln firings that cool slowly overnight, raku pieces are lifted red-hot from the gas kiln at nine hundred degrees with long iron tongs and placed straight into metal bins filled with dry sawdust.

Because of that extreme thermal shock, bowls thrown from smooth porcelain clay will shatter almost immediately. Every piece you bring on Saturday must already be bisque-fired using coarse grogged raku clay, whose tiny pre-fired sand particles open microscopic pathways for steam and heat to escape safely. Maximum height is eighteen centimeters so four pots fit per load.

For safety around glowing tongs and smoke, synthetic fleece jackets and nylon running shoes are not allowed near the kiln pad; please wear long-sleeved cotton denim, leather closed-toe shoes, and hair ties.

Makoto Hori
passage.translation: 陶芸部顧問の堀誠先生から楽焼（らくやき）実習参加者へのメール。今週土曜午前9時半から美術室裏で屋外の楽焼焼成を行う。一晩かけてゆっくり冷ます通常の電気窯とは異なり、楽焼では900度に赤熱した器を長い鉄ばさみでガス窯から直接取り出し、乾いたおがくず入りの金属缶へ入れる。急激な熱衝撃がかかるため、滑らかな磁器土で作った茶碗はほぼ確実に割れてしまう。土曜に持参する作品はすべて、微細な焼き砂（シャモット）を含み蒸気や熱を逃がしやすい粗めの楽焼用粘土で素焼き済みのものに限る（1回に4点入るよう高さ18センチ以内）。安全のため化学繊維のフリースやナイロン靴は窯場近くで禁止とし、綿デニムの長袖、つま先の覆われた革靴、髪留めを着用すること。

items.prompt: Why must participants use coarse grogged raku clay rather than smooth porcelain clay?
choices: Grogged raku clay requires no bisque firing before Saturday's workshop.
Coarse grogged clay turns bright cobalt blue without any glaze.
Sand particles in grogged clay vent steam safely without shattering pots.
Smooth porcelain clay melts long iron tongs at room temperature.
items.explanation: smooth porcelain clay will shatter almost immediately ... coarse grogged raku clay, whose tiny pre-fired sand particles open microscopic pathways for steam and heat to escape safelyとある。
distractorReasons: 素焼き不要とは逆（already be bisque-firedが必要）。
釉薬なしで青くなる話ではない。
砂粒（シャモット）が蒸気と熱の逃げ道をつくり急冷時の破損を防ぐため。
常温で鉄ばさみが溶けることはない。
items.translation: 滑らかな磁器土ではなく粗めのシャモット入り楽焼粘土を使わなければならないのはなぜですか。

choices: Wear breathable nylon tracksuits and open-toed sport sandals outdoors.

Change into shared rubber studio clogs lined up beside the kiln gate.

distractorReasons: ナイロン製ジャージやつま先の開いたサンダルは火花で溶ける・火傷するため厳禁。
化学繊維を避け、綿の長袖と革靴を着用する。
ポリエステル等の化学繊維フリースは熱で溶ける危険があるため不可。
共用ゴムサンダルではなく自分の革靴・キャンバス靴と綿の長袖を着用する。
items.translation: 土曜日の窯場近くではどのような服装ルールを守る必要がありますか。

items.prompt: One problem mentioned in the passage is that
choices: seamless vinyl floor tiles wore out quickly under heavy medicine carts.
acoustic ceiling panels muffled urgent bedside emergency alarms too much.
long straight hallways prevented nurses from monitoring distant room doors.
hard parallel surfaces reflected footsteps, carts, and beeps far down the ward, disrupting sleep.
items.explanation: hard parallel walls bounce footsteps, pager beeps, and rolling cart clatter down the entire ward, pushing nighttime decibel levels far above ... guidelinesとある。
distractorReasons: ビニル床タイルの摩耗の早さが問題だったのではない。
緊急アラームまで聞こえなくなったのではなく硬い反射面で音が響きすぎた。
直線廊下は見通し自体は良かったが音のトンネルになっていた。
第1段落の反響・夜間騒音超過の説明と一致。
items.translation: 1970年代の直線的な病院廊下において、研究者はどのような音響上の問題を発見しましたか。

passage.title: Why Hospital Architects Replace Long Echoing Halls
passage.text:
Step into a hospital ward built in the 1970s, and its floor plan usually follows a "racetrack" or single straight corridor stretching sixty meters from end to end, lined with glossy vinyl tiles and hard plaster ceilings. Architects back then prized unbroken sightlines and easy mopping. Acoustic measurements conducted over the past twenty years, however, revealed an unintended side effect: hard parallel walls bounce footsteps, pager beeps, and rolling cart clatter down the entire ward, pushing nighttime decibel levels far above World Health Organization guidelines for restorative sleep.

Elevated ward noise harms more than patient comfort. Sleep studies in cardiac and surgical recovery units show that repeated fifty-five-decibel noise spikes trigger brief surges in heart rate and stress hormones even when patients do not consciously recall waking up. Fragmented rest slows immune recovery and makes delirium more common among older adults. Nurses suffer too: in reverberant corridors where conversations blur together, staff report higher mental fatigue and must double-check spoken medication numbers more carefully to prevent misheard doses.

Modern hospital designers now attack corridor noise through both geometry and materials. Instead of one unbroken tunnel, wards are divided into shorter decentralized clusters curved gently around small nursing alcoves, cutting the distance sound can travel unchecked. Overhead, micro-perforated mineral tiles swallow speech frequencies while still meeting strict infection-control wiping standards, and poured rubber subfloors cushion stretcher wheels.

Several Scandinavian and Japanese teaching hospitals have paired structural redesign with "quiet-night protocols"—switching nurse call alerts from corridor loudspeakers to vibrating wrist badges after 9:00 p.m. and grouping routine blood-pressure checks so sleeping patients are disturbed less often.

Healing requires skilled medicine, yet architecture that guards quiet rest turns every night on the ward into part of the treatment.
passage.translation: 1970年代に建てられた病棟に入ると、端から端まで60メートルも続く一直線の廊下に光沢のあるビニル床と硬い天井が並んでいることがよくあります。見通しの良さと清掃性を優先した設計でしたが、近年の音響測定により、硬い平行壁が足音やナースコール、カートの走行音を病棟全体に反響させ、夜間の騒音値がWHOの安眠指針を大きく上回っていることが分かりました。55デシベル前後の突発音が繰り返されると、患者が自覚的に目覚めなくても心拍数やストレスホルモンが上昇し、免疫回復の遅れや高齢患者のせん妄リスクを高めます。看護師側も反響する廊下では疲労が増し、口頭の投薬量確認に余計な神経を使います。そこで現代の病院建築は、長い一直線の廊下を緩やかに曲がる小規模クラスターへ分割して音の直進を遮り、消毒基準を満たす微細孔吸音天井やゴム系下地床を採用しています。さらに北欧や日本の大学病院では午後9時以降のコール通知を廊下スピーカーから振動リストバンドへ切り替える「静音夜間運用」も組み合わせ、建築と運用の両面から静かな眠りを治療の一部として守っています。

items.prompt: According to the second paragraph, how do nighttime noise spikes affect recovering patients?
choices: They prompt light sleepers in shared rooms to request ear plugs or evening sedatives.
They disrupt deep REM cycles mainly after four a.m. when hallway carts start rolling.
They cause brief jumps in heart rate and stress hormones even without conscious awakening, slowing recovery.
They raise perceived pain scores among surgical patients resting near central elevators.
items.explanation: trigger brief surges in heart rate and stress hormones even when patients do not consciously recall waking up. Fragmented rest slows immune recoveryとある。
distractorReasons: 強い睡眠薬の処方希望が増えるという説明ではない。
昼間の待合ラウンジではなく夜間の入院患者の回復への悪影響。
第2段落の生理的影響と一致。
早朝の申し送り時間帯だけの問題ではない。
items.translation: 第2段落によると、夜間の突発的な騒音は回復期の患者にどのような影響を与えますか。

items.prompt: How do modern hospital architects reduce how far noise travels along a ward?
choices: By fitting automatic double-glazed sliding doors every ten meters along straight ward corridors.

By playing soft acoustic masking chimes through ceiling speakers outside patient room doorways.
By breaking long halls into shorter, gently curved clusters paired with sound-absorbing ceilings and rubber subfloors.
items.explanation: wards are divided into shorter decentralized clusters curved gently ... micro-perforated mineral tiles ... poured rubber subfloorsとある。

ナースステーションをすべて地下階に隔離する設計ではない（分散配置）。

items.prompt: What operational change is part of the "quiet-night protocols" mentioned in paragraph four?
choices: Sending nighttime call alerts to nurses' vibrating wrist badges instead of overhead speakers.

passage.title: Why Hospital Architects Replace Long Echoing Halls
passage.text:
Step into a hospital ward built in the 1970s, and its floor plan usually follows a "racetrack" or single straight corridor stretching sixty meters from end to end, lined with glossy vinyl tiles and hard plaster ceilings. Architects back then prized unbroken sightlines and easy mopping. Acoustic measurements conducted over the past twenty years, however, revealed an unintended side effect: hard parallel walls bounce footsteps, pager beeps, and rolling cart clatter down the entire ward, pushing nighttime decibel levels far above World Health Organization guidelines for restorative sleep.

Elevated ward noise harms more than patient comfort. Sleep studies in cardiac and surgical recovery units show that repeated fifty-five-decibel noise spikes trigger brief surges in heart rate and stress hormones even when patients do not consciously recall waking up. Fragmented rest slows immune recovery and makes delirium more common among older adults. Nurses suffer too: in reverberant corridors where conversations blur together, staff report higher mental fatigue and must double-check spoken medication numbers more carefully to prevent misheard doses.

Modern hospital designers now attack corridor noise through both geometry and materials. Instead of one unbroken tunnel, wards are divided into shorter decentralized clusters curved gently around small nursing alcoves, cutting the distance sound can travel unchecked. Overhead, micro-perforated mineral tiles swallow speech frequencies while still meeting strict infection-control wiping standards, and poured rubber subfloors cushion stretcher wheels.

Several Scandinavian and Japanese teaching hospitals have paired structural redesign with "quiet-night protocols"—switching nurse call alerts from corridor loudspeakers to vibrating wrist badges after 9:00 p.m. and grouping routine blood-pressure checks so sleeping patients are disturbed less often.

Healing requires skilled medicine, yet architecture that guards quiet rest turns every night on the ward into part of the treatment.

passage.title: Why Stadiums Leave Wind Gaps Under Their Roofs
passage.text:
Watch an evening soccer match inside a modern European or Japanese stadium, and you will notice a dramatic architectural frame: a sweeping roof shelters almost every spectator seat from rain, yet stops abruptly around a wide open oculus above the grass pitch—while slotted gaps also pierce the lower wall behind corner flags. Fans sometimes wish builders had sealed the bowl completely against cold wind, yet turf agronomists insist those carefully modeled air vents keep natural grass alive.

Championship soccer requires resilient living grass whose roots knit sandy soil together when players pivot at full sprint. Semi-enclosed stadium roofs, however, cast deep midday shadows across the southern touchline and trap humid air exhaled by fifty thousand spectators. Without steady breeze skimming across the blades, morning dew and irrigation water linger all day, inviting fungal turf diseases that can rot an entire penalty box within forty-eight hours. (18), stagnant air starves grass leaves of fresh carbon dioxide during sunny hours.

Wind-tunnel engineers therefore test scale stadium models with smoke streams before steel fabrication begins. Low wall louvers draw cool street-level air across the pitch and vent warm moist air upward through the roof opening by natural convection. On calm winter weeks when clouds block sunlight too, groundskeepers wheel out mobile LED grow-light rigs and low-noise turf fans to supplement nature. (19), sensors buried beneath the center circle monitor root-zone moisture and salt buildup hour by hour.

What looks like an unfinished gap between wall and roof actually reflects how modern stadium design (20).
passage.translation: 現代のヨーロッパや日本のサッカースタジアムでナイターを観戦すると、観客席のほぼすべてを雨から守る大屋根が芝生のピッチ上空で大きく口を開け、さらにコーナーフラッグ裏の低い壁にもスリット状の通風口が設けられていることに気づきます。寒い風が入らないよう完全に密閉してほしいと思う観客もいますが、芝生管理の専門家に言わせれば、この計算された風の通り道こそ天然芝を生かす生命線なのです。高い屋根に囲まれたスタジアムは南側タッチライン付近に濃い日陰をつくり、5万人の観客が出す湿気もこもらせます。葉面をなでる風がなければ朝露や散水が一日中乾かず、わずか48時間でペナルティエリアの芝を腐らせる糸状菌病を招きます。(18)、よどんだ空気は日中の光合成に必要な二酸化炭素の供給も滞らせます。そのため設計段階から風洞実験で低い壁のルーバーから屋根開口へ抜ける自然対流をつくり、日照不足の冬には移動式LED補光機や送風機も併用します。(19)、センターサークル下のセンサーが根域の水分と塩分を毎時監視しています。壁と屋根の隙間は、(20)設計の結晶なのです。

distractorReasons: 以前は、ではない。
逆に、ではない。

passage.title: Why Stadiums Leave Wind Gaps Under Their Roofs
passage.text:
Watch an evening soccer match inside a modern European or Japanese stadium, and you will notice a dramatic architectural frame: a sweeping roof shelters almost every spectator seat from rain, yet stops abruptly around a wide open oculus above the grass pitch—while slotted gaps also pierce the lower wall behind corner flags. Fans sometimes wish builders had sealed the bowl completely against cold wind, yet turf agronomists insist those carefully modeled air vents keep natural grass alive.

Championship soccer requires resilient living grass whose roots knit sandy soil together when players pivot at full sprint. Semi-enclosed stadium roofs, however, cast deep midday shadows across the southern touchline and trap humid air exhaled by fifty thousand spectators. Without steady breeze skimming across the blades, morning dew and irrigation water linger all day, inviting fungal turf diseases that can rot an entire penalty box within forty-eight hours. (18), stagnant air starves grass leaves of fresh carbon dioxide during sunny hours.

Wind-tunnel engineers therefore test scale stadium models with smoke streams before steel fabrication begins. Low wall louvers draw cool street-level air across the pitch and vent warm moist air upward through the roof opening by natural convection. On calm winter weeks when clouds block sunlight too, groundskeepers wheel out mobile LED grow-light rigs and low-noise turf fans to supplement nature. (19), sensors buried beneath the center circle monitor root-zone moisture and salt buildup hour by hour.

What looks like an unfinished gap between wall and roof actually reflects how modern stadium design (20).

passage.title: Why Libraries Digitize Local Ephemera
passage.text:
When people picture historical treasures preserved in library vaults, they usually imagine leather-bound diaries of prime ministers, medieval maps, or first-edition novels. Yet social historians trying to reconstruct how ordinary families shopped, commuted, and celebrated eighty years ago often find grand official books frustratingly silent. Increasingly, municipal libraries are scanning fragile everyday paper—"ephemera" never meant to survive more than a week—such as tram tickets, neighborhood festival handbills, department-store lunch menus, and rationing coupons.

Printed on cheap acidic wood-pulp paper, ephemera yellows and crumbles far faster than rag-paper books if left in attic shoeboxes. Once digitized with high-resolution overhead cameras and tagged by street name and year, however, a single box of 1950s grocery flyers unlocks vivid economic history: researchers can compare seasonal sardine prices against factory wages, trace when electric rice cookers entered working-class kitchens, or spot vanished cinema names along a suburban shopping arcade. (21), retired residents invited to library "scan-and-share" Saturdays often supply the spoken context behind a faded ticket stub before memories fade.

Curating everyday paper still demands selective judgment. Libraries lack server space and staff hours to scan fifty identical bus timetables from the same month, so archivists sample representative items across diverse districts rather than only wealthy downtown streets. (22), privacy rules require redacting personal medical receipts or living individuals' home addresses before posting scans online.

Fragile handbills and menus may look disposable, yet preserving them gives future generations (23).
passage.translation: 図書館の貴重書庫といえば首相の革装日記や古地図、初版本を思い浮かべがちですが、80年前のごく普通の家族が何を食べ、どう通勤し、どんな祭りを祝っていたかを調べようとする社会史家にとって、立派な公文書は驚くほど多くを語ってくれません。そこで今、各地の公立図書館が力を入れているのが、本来1週間ほどで捨てられるはずだった路面電車の切符、町内祭りのチラシ、百貨店食堂のメニューといった「エフェメラ（短命印刷物）」のデジタル保存です。安価な酸性紙に刷られたチラシ類は屋根裏の靴箱に置かれたままだとボロボロに崩れますが、高精細カメラで撮影し通り名や年代タグを付ければ、1950年代の特売チラシ1箱から当時のイワシの値段と工場賃金の比較や電気炊飯器の普及時期、消えた映画館の名前まで鮮やかに浮かび上がります。(21)、土曜の持ち寄りスキャン会に招かれた高齢住民が、色あせた半券にまつわる記憶を語り残してくれます。もちろん同じ月のバス時刻表を50部も保存する余裕はないため幅広い地区から代表資料を選び、(22)、公開前には現存個人の住所などを伏せる配慮も欠かせません。一見使い捨ての紙片を守ることは、未来の世代に(23)を届ける営みなのです。

items.prompt: Why is measuring snow depth with a ruler alone insufficient for judging roof safety?
choices: Aluminum depth poles contract slightly in subzero wind and underreport deep roof drifts.
Steep eaves cause windblown snow to pile unevenly away from fixed roof measurement stakes.
Older timber rafters lose strength when attic heat melts the bottom centimeter of snow.
Equal depths of fluffy powder and rain-soaked snow differ greatly in actual weight on roof rafters.

吹きだまりで測れないからではなく雪質（密度）によって重さが何倍も違うため。
乾いた新雪10センチで折れるからではない。
同じ40センチでも新雪と雨を含んだ雪では実際の荷重が大きく異なるため。
items.translation: 屋根の安全性を判断するうえで、物差しで積雪の深さだけを測るのでは不十分なのはなぜですか。

passage.title: Guidelines for Borrowing Roof-Snow Measurement Kits
passage.text:
From: Kitano Town Winter Safety Division
To: Neighborhood Association Snow Wardens
Subject: Calibrating borrowed snow-core tubes before December patrols

Dear Snow Wardens,
Thank you for volunteering to monitor roof-snow loads on elderly residents' homes this winter. Measuring snow depth with a ruler alone can be dangerously misleading: forty centimeters of fluffy January powder weighs far less than forty centimeters of rain-soaked February pack, which can quietly overload older timber rafters.

Starting Monday, each district warden may pick up a lightweight aluminum snow-core tube and hanging spring scale at Town Hall Annex Room 104. Push the hollow tube straight down to the roof eaves marker, lift out a vertical cylinder of snow, and weigh it on the hook scale to read water-equivalent load in kilograms per square meter.

Before every morning patrol, hang the empty dry tube on the scale and turn the top brass ring until the pointer reads exactly zero; trapped ice inside the barrel will inflate readings. Please log figures on the shared tablet form by noon.

Winter Safety Division
passage.translation: 北野町冬季安全課から各町内会の雪害見回り担当者へのメール。高齢世帯の屋根雪荷重の見回り協力に感謝する。物差しで積雪の「深さ」だけを測るのは危険な誤認を招く。1月のふわふわした新雪40センチと、2月の雨を含んだ締まり雪40センチでは重さがまったく異なり、後者は古い木造垂木に過大な負荷をかけかねない。月曜から役場別館104室でアルミ製採雪管と吊りばね秤を貸し出す。中空の管を軒先の標識板まで垂直に差し込んで円柱状の雪を抜き取り、秤に吊るして1平方メートルあたりの水当量荷重（kg）を読み取ること。毎朝の見回り前には必ず空の乾いた管を秤に吊るし、上部の真鍮リングを回して針を正確にゼロに合わせること（管内に氷が残っていると数値が高く出てしまう）。数値は正午までに共有タブレット入力フォームへ記録してほしい。

items.prompt: How must wardens calibrate the spring scale before each morning patrol?
choices: Hang the empty dry tube on the scale and turn the brass ring until the pointer reads zero.
Compare the spring scale reading against a digital scale inside the office.
Cool the aluminum sampling tube in a snowbank for ten minutes before weighing.
Fill the cylinder halfway with tap water to check the one-kilogram mark.
items.explanation: Before every morning patrol, hang the empty dry tube on the scale and turn the top brass ring until the pointer reads exactly zeroとある。
distractorReasons: 空の乾いた採雪管を吊るし、真鍮リングを回してゼロ点調整する。
事務室のデジタル秤と毎回照合する手順ではない。
測定前に雪山で10分冷やす手順はゼロ点調整ではない（採取前の付着防止とは別）。
水道水を入れて1kg目盛りを確認する手順ではない。
items.translation: 毎朝の見回り前に、担当者はばね秤をどのようにゼロ点調整しなければなりませんか。

passage.translation: 北野町冬季安全課から各町内会の雪害見回り担当者へのメール。高齢世帯の屋根雪荷重の見回り協力に感謝する。物差しで積雪の「深さ」だけを測るのは危険な誤認を招く。1月のふわふわした新雪40センチと、2月の雨を含んだ締まり雪40センチでは重さがまったく異なり、後者は古い木造垂木に過大な負荷をかけかねない。月曜から役場別館104室でアルミ製採雪管と吊りばね秤を貸し出す。中空の管を軒先の標識板まで垂直に差し込んで円柱状の雪を抜き取り、秤に吊るして1平方メートルあたりの水当量荷重（kg）を読み取ること。毎朝の見回り前には必ず空の乾いた管を秤に吊るし、上部の真鍮リングを回して針を正確にゼロに合わせること（管内に氷が残っていると数値が高く出てしまう）。数値は正午までに共有タブレット入力フォームへ記録してほしい。

items.prompt: What physical property of soil ten to fifty meters underground makes ground-source heat pumps effective?
choices: Subterranean mineral springs warm deep gravel beds twenty degrees above winter air.
Slow groundwater flow carries summer warmth beneath suburban streets until February.
Its temperature stays steady around ten to fifteen degrees all year despite surface weather swings.
Dense clay layers trap household heat escaping downward from insulated basements.

distractorReasons: 非火山地域でも50度以上の蒸気があるわけではない。
地下河川が温風を運ぶからではない。
第1段落の地中温度の年間安定性の説明と一致。
30度以上になるのではなく年間を通じて10〜15度前後の安定した温度を保つ。
items.translation: 地下10〜50メートルの土壌がもつどのような物理的特性が、地中熱ヒートポンプを有効にしていますか。

passage.title: How Geothermal Heat Pumps Tap Steady Ground Warmth
passage.text:
Ask homeowners in snowy Hokkaido or northern Europe how they heat rooms in January without burning kerosene or natural gas, and a growing number point downward rather than toward the sky. Ground-source (or geothermal) heat pumps exploit that quiet thermal stability without needing volcanic hot springs. Contractors drill narrow vertical boreholes beside a house or school and lower sealed plastic U-tubes filled with water and nontoxic antifreeze. In winter, circulating fluid absorbs modest warmth from the surrounding earth and carries it indoors, where an electric compressor concentrates that heat to warm floor pipes or radiators. Because moving existing warmth takes far less electricity than generating heat from scratch with resistance coils, a well-designed ground loop delivers roughly four units of indoor heat for every single unit of electrical energy consumed.

Better still, the cycle reverses effortlessly in July. Instead of struggling to dump indoor heat into thirty-five-degree street air the way ordinary outdoor air-conditioner units must, a ground-source pump sends surplus room heat down into cool twelve-degree earth—trimming summer cooling bills while gently recharging soil warmth for the coming winter.

Why, then, has ground-source heating not replaced every furnace overnight? Drilling fifty-meter boreholes requires specialized rigs that struggle to enter cramped urban alleys, and upfront installation can cost two to three times as much as an air-source heat pump, taking a decade of lower utility bills to pay back.

To hurdle that barrier, several municipalities and housing developers now build shared neighborhood ground loops beneath parks or parking lots, letting individual households hook into steady underground warmth for a predictable monthly fee.
passage.translation: 雪深い北海道や北欧で灯油やガスを燃やさずに1月の室内を暖める方法を尋ねると、空ではなく「地面の下」を指さす家庭が増えています。冬の気温は昼と深夜氷点下15度のあいだで激しく変動しますが、凍結深度より下の地下10〜50メートルの土壌や岩盤は、大地そのものが巨大な魔法瓶となって一年中ほぼ一定の10〜15度を保っています。地中熱ヒートポンプは火山性の温泉がなくてもこの安定した温度差を活用します。建物の横に細い垂直ボアホールを掘って不凍液入りの密閉U字管を埋め、冬は地中の穏やかな熱をくみ上げて電気コンプレッサーで濃縮し床暖房などに送ります。ゼロから電熱線で発熱するよりはるかに少ない電力で済むため、消費電力1に対して約4倍の温熱を得られます。さらに7月には運転を逆転させ、35度の外気へ苦労して排熱する通常のエアコン室外機と違い、12度の涼しい地中へ室内の熱を逃がして冷房費を抑えつつ冬に向けた蓄熱も行えます。普及の壁は掘削機が狭い路地に入りにくいことと初期費用が空気熱式の2〜3倍かかる点ですが、近年は公園や駐車場の下に地域共有の地中熱ループを整備し、各世帯が定額で利用できる取り組みも始まっています。

items.prompt: Why does a ground-source heat pump use much less electricity than an electric resistance heater?
choices: Deep vertical loops tap warm groundwater veins to heat radiator water without compressors.
Insulated backyard boreholes store surplus rooftop solar heat collected during late summer.
Variable-speed circulation pumps run chiefly overnight when off-peak grid power is cheap.
Moving and concentrating existing ground warmth requires far less electrical energy than creating heat from scratch.
items.explanation: Because moving existing warmth takes far less electricity than generating heat from scratch with resistance coils ... four units of indoor heat for every single unit of electrical energyとある。
distractorReasons: 火山蒸気を直接引き込む地熱発電地帯限定の仕組みではない。
夏の屋根集熱をタンクに貯める太陽熱システムではない。
夜間電力料金の安さではなく「熱を一から作らず地中の安定した熱を移動・濃縮する」物理的効率の高さが理由。
第2段落のヒートポンプ効率の原理と一致。
items.translation: 地中熱ヒートポンプが電気抵抗ヒーターよりはるかに少ない電力で済むのはなぜですか。

items.prompt: How does the underground loop benefit a building during hot July weather?
choices: It enters low-power standby until outdoor temperatures drop in November.
It dumps indoor heat into cool twelve-degree earth far more efficiently.
It circulates cool cellar air through floor vents without running fans.
It preheats domestic tap water using surplus warmth from attic roofs.
items.explanation: Instead of struggling to dump indoor heat into thirty-five-degree street air ... sends surplus room heat down into cool twelve-degree earthとある。
distractorReasons: 12月まで停止するのではない。
第3段落の夏期冷房・地中放熱の仕組みと一致。
窓を凍らせるのではない。
泥水散布ではない。
items.translation: 暑い7月の時期に、地下ループは建物にどのような恩恵をもたらしますか。

items.prompt: What main obstacle has slowed widespread adoption of individual ground-source systems?
choices: Drilling boreholes requires heavy rigs and high upfront costs that take years to recover.
Horizontal garden trenches lose half their heating output whenever frost reaches thirty centimeters.
Buried polyethylene loops require specialized chemical flushing every third autumn.
Narrow urban lots lack space for indoor heat-exchange cabinets near water heaters.
items.explanation: Drilling fifty-meter boreholes requires specialized rigs that struggle to enter cramped urban alleys, and upfront installation can cost two to three times as muchとある。
distractorReasons: 第4段落の掘削スペース制約と初期費用の高さに一致。
屋根の積雪で止まることはない。
2冬で管が溶けるとはない。
電力4倍は逆（1の電力で4の熱）。
items.translation: 戸別の地中熱システムの急速な普及を妨げてきた主な障壁は何ですか。

items.prompt: According to the passage, some municipalities and developers are helping households overcome high installation costs
choices: by offering low-interest municipal loans to homeowners who share a mobile drilling rig.
by building shared neighborhood ground loops under parks or parking lots with monthly connection fees.
by recovering waste heat from municipal subway tunnels and piping it to nearby homes.
by requiring new suburban housing estates to pre-drill vertical loops before paving roads.

最終段落の地域共有地中熱ループの取り組みと一致。
公衆浴場の排水を回す仕組みではなく公園や駐車場の下に共有地中熱ループを埋設する。

items.translation: 一部の自治体や開発事業者は、高い初期費用を乗り越えるためどのような支援策を講じていますか。

items.prompt: To protect nesting plovers along the gravel spit, beachgoers are asked to (     ) from flying kites or drones between April and July.
items.explanation: 砂州で営巣するチドリを守るため、4月から7月のあいだ凧やドローンを飛ばすのを「差し控える・遠慮する」よう求められているrefrain from doing。
distractorReasons: undergoは「経験する・受ける」で文脈に合わない。
facilitateは「促進する」で文脈に合わない。
refrain from -ingで〜するのを控える。
diminishは「減少させる」で文脈に合わない。

items.prompt:
A: The mountain weather station operates without resident staff.
B: Even so, its satellite transmitter sends snowpack data (     ) every fifteen minutes.
items.explanation: 常駐職員のいない無人山岳気象観測所だが、衛星送信機が15分ごとに積雪データを「確実に・安定して」送信しているsends data reliably。
distractorReasons: explicitlyは「明示的に」で文脈に合わない。
virtuallyは「事実上」で文脈に合わない。
simultaneouslyは「同時に」で文脈に合わない。
reliablyは高い信頼性で確実に。Although（無人であるにもかかわらず）と自然に対応。

A: Handmade rice paper blurs easily if ink pools.
B: Yes, so calligraphers practice (     ) brush pressure smoothly at the end of every stroke.

fosteringは「育む」で文脈に合わない。
curbingは「抑制する」で文脈に合わない。

passage.title: Why Concert Pianists Care About Bench Height
passage.text:
Watch a solo pianist walk onstage before a concerto, and you may see the performer spend thirty seconds turning dual side knobs on the padded bench—testing a single chord, rising slightly, and adjusting the seat by barely half a centimeter before nodding to the conductor. Audience members sometimes read this ritual as nervous perfectionism, yet biomechanics specialists say millimeter changes in bench height transform both tone production and injury risk.

Unlike typing at an office laptop, playing grand-piano repertoire demands transferring upper-body weight fluidly through relaxed shoulders, forearms, and finger pads into eighty-eight weighted wooden keys. If a bench sits two centimeters too low, a pianist must shrug the shoulders upward or bend the wrists below key level, choking leverage during thunderous chords and straining forearm tendons over two-hour programs. (18), perching too high forces the player to hunch forward, tiring lower-back muscles and making delicate soft passages harder to control.

Pedal geometry complicates the equation further. Taller pianists with long legs often push the bench slightly farther back from the keyboard so their right ankle can pivot smoothly on the damper pedal without cramping, which in turn changes elbow angles at the keys. Backstage technicians at major halls therefore keep numbered hydraulic or screw benches logged by artist preference. (19), traveling soloists who play different pianos every week carry a pocket tape measure to match seat-to-key distance precisely.

Those quiet turns of a bench knob before the first note show how musical artistry (20).
passage.translation: 協奏曲の開演前、ステージに現れたピアニストが椅子の両脇のノブを30秒ほど回し、和音を一つ鳴らしてはわずか5ミリ座面を上下させてから指揮者にうなずく光景を目にすることがあります。神経質なこだわりに見えるかもしれませんが、身体運動学の専門家に言わせれば、わずか数ミリの座面高の違いが音色の響きと故障リスクの両方を大きく左右します。グランドピアノの演奏は、脱力した肩と前腕から指先へと上半身の重みを88鍵へ滑らかに伝える全身運動です。椅子が2センチ低すぎるだけで肩がすくみ手首が鍵盤より下がって力強い和音のてこが効かず腱を痛めやすくなります。(18)、高すぎれば前かがみになって腰が疲れ、繊細な弱音の制御が難しくなります。さらにペダルを踏む足首の角度との兼ね合いもあるため、主要ホールの舞台裏では演奏家ごとの好みの高さを記録しており、(19)、毎週違う会場で弾くソリストはポケット巻尺を持ち歩いて座面と鍵盤の高低差を正確に揃えます。開演前の静かな微調整は、音楽表現が(20)ことを物語っているのです。

passage.title: How Floating Solar Panels Help Water Reservoirs
passage.text:
Countries rich in sunshine often face a painful land-use dilemma as renewable energy expands: flat sunny valleys ideal for ground-mounted solar farms are frequently the very fields most prized for growing rice, vegetables, or orchard fruit. Over the past decade, water authorities in Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and California have found clever relief on surfaces already shaped by human engineering—agricultural irrigation ponds and municipal drinking-water reservoirs.

By mooring buoyant high-density polyethylene pontoons across ten to thirty percent of an artificial reservoir, utilities create "floatovoltaics" without felling a single forest tree or displacing a farm plot. Water and silicon panels form a mutually beneficial match. Just as rooftop vegetation cools air beneath panels, open water underneath floating arrays moderates summer operating temperatures, boosting electrical yield during heat waves. (21), shading part of the reservoir surface cuts wind-driven evaporation—saving thousands of cubic meters of precious irrigation water during dry summers—and limits sunlight that fuels foul-tasting blue-green algae blooms.

Engineers are careful not to blanket natural lakes wholesale. Covering an entire natural pond could block oxygen exchange or disturb diving waterfowl, so floating arrays are steered toward lined industrial basins, quarry lakes, and dam reservoirs, leaving wide shoreline zones open. (22), cables and anchors must be designed to ride five-meter seasonal water-level swings without chafing.

Used thoughtfully on human-made waters, floating solar arrays allow regions short on flat land to (23).

passage.title: How Floating Solar Panels Help Water Reservoirs
passage.text:
Countries rich in sunshine often face a painful land-use dilemma as renewable energy expands: flat sunny valleys ideal for ground-mounted solar farms are frequently the very fields most prized for growing rice, vegetables, or orchard fruit. Over the past decade, water authorities in Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and California have found clever relief on surfaces already shaped by human engineering—agricultural irrigation ponds and municipal drinking-water reservoirs.

By mooring buoyant high-density polyethylene pontoons across ten to thirty percent of an artificial reservoir, utilities create "floatovoltaics" without felling a single forest tree or displacing a farm plot. Water and silicon panels form a mutually beneficial match. Just as rooftop vegetation cools air beneath panels, open water underneath floating arrays moderates summer operating temperatures, boosting electrical yield during heat waves. (21), shading part of the reservoir surface cuts wind-driven evaporation—saving thousands of cubic meters of precious irrigation water during dry summers—and limits sunlight that fuels foul-tasting blue-green algae blooms.

Engineers are careful not to blanket natural lakes wholesale. Covering an entire natural pond could block oxygen exchange or disturb diving waterfowl, so floating arrays are steered toward lined industrial basins, quarry lakes, and dam reservoirs, leaving wide shoreline zones open. (22), cables and anchors must be designed to ride five-meter seasonal water-level swings without chafing.

passage.title: Costume Laundry Rules After the Autumn Opera Run
passage.text:
From: Wardrobe Mistress, Naomi Kudo
To: Student Chorus and Stage Crew
Subject: Returning velvet tunics and wool cloaks after Sunday's final curtain

Congratulations on three sold-out performances! Before everyone rushes home after Sunday's matinee curtain call, please read this important costume-care reminder.

Please do NOT take your velvet chorus tunic or lined wool cloak home to wash in a household machine, even on a gentle cold cycle. Water shrinks wool interlinings unevenly and crushes velvet pile permanently, which cost our theater club four bespoke jackets two years ago.

Instead, hang your costume inside-out on its numbered wooden hanger right after changing, clip any loose buttons into the small mesh pouch on the hook, and leave it on the rolling rack outside Dressing Room B by 5:30 p.m. Our costume vendor will dry-clean all outer garments together on Monday. Washable cotton undershirts, however, should go home with you and return clean on Thursday.

Naomi Kudo
passage.translation: 衣装担当の工藤直美さんから学生合唱団・舞台スタッフへのメール。3公演完売おめでとう。日曜マチネ（昼公演）のカーテンコール後に帰宅する前に衣装返却ルールを確認してほしい。ベルベットの合唱チュニックや裏地付きウールマントは、たとえ弱水流・水洗いコースであっても自宅の洗濯機で絶対に洗わないこと。水洗いでウールの芯地が不均一に縮みベルベットの毛並みも潰れてしまい、2年前には特注ジャケット4着が駄目になった。着替えたらすぐに衣装を裏返して番号付き木製ハンガーに掛け、取れかけたボタンがあればフックの小メッシュ袋に入れ、午後5時半までに楽屋B前の移動ラックへ戻すこと。外衣はすべて月曜に専門業者がまとめてドライクリーニングする。なお水洗い可能な綿の肌着だけは各自持ち帰って洗濯し、木曜に返却すること。

passage.title: How Porous Pavement Tames Urban Flash Floods
passage.text:
When an intense summer thunderstorm dumps fifty millimeters of rain onto a forested hillside, spongy leaf litter and tree-root channels soak up most of the downpour, releasing clear water slowly into streams over days. Drop that same cloudburst onto a conventional city neighborhood—where roofs, parking lots, and asphalt streets seal eighty percent of the ground—and rainwater has nowhere to sink. Torrents race across oily pavement into storm drains within minutes, overwhelming sewer pipes, flooding underpasses, and flushing tire dust and litter straight into urban rivers.

Rather than digging ever-wider concrete storm tunnels beneath crowded streets, civil engineers are redesigning pavement itself to mimic forest soil. Conventional asphalt and concrete mix coarse gravel with fine sand that packs every tiny gap shut. Pervious concrete and porous asphalt, by contrast, deliberately omit fine sand particles, leaving an interconnected honeycomb of air voids—roughly twenty percent of the slab's volume—through which rainwater drains straight downward into a thick crushed-stone reservoir bed underneath.

Beneath parking bays, plazas, and low-speed residential lanes, that gravel bed acts as both sponge and biofilter. Stormwater pauses among irregular stone surfaces for hours before seeping into native subsoil or perforated overflow pipes, shaving dangerous flood peaks during cloudbursts. Meanwhile, naturally occurring bacteria coating the stones break down trace motor-oil hydrocarbons, and cooler moisture evaporating after storms trims surface pavement heat.

Porous surfaces are not maintenance-free miracles, nor do they suit eighty-kilometer-per-hour truck highways where heavy braking shears open-graded stone loose. Without semiannual cleaning by vacuum sweeper trucks, windblown silt and autumn leaves can clog surface pores within a few years—and well-meaning crews must never sealcoat porous lots with black tar.

Matched to the right streets and upkeep schedules, however, permeable paving turns acres of hard city crust back into living watershed.
passage.translation: 夏の激しい雷雨が森林の斜面に50ミリの雨を降らせても、ふかふかの落葉層と木の根の隙間が大半を吸い込み、数日かけて澄んだ水を小川へ送り出します。ところが屋根や駐車場、アスファルト道路が地面の8割を塞ぐ従来の市街地に同じ豪雨が降ると、雨水は行き場を失って数分で雨水ますへ殺到し、アンダーパスの冠水や河川へのタイヤ粉塵流出を引き起こします。地下の排水管を際限なく太く掘り直す代わりに、土木技術者たちは舗装そのものに森の土を模倣させ始めました。通常の舗装と違い細かい砂をあえて抜いた「透水性コンクリート・排水性アスファルト」は体積の約2割が連続した空隙になっており、雨水をそのまま下の厚い砕石貯留層へと逃がします。駐車場や広場、生活道路の下に敷かれた砕石層は豪雨の一時貯留スポンジとして洪水のピークを削るだけでなく、石の表面に棲む微生物が微量の油分を分解する浄化フィルターにもなります。もっとも高速で大型トラックが急制動する幹線道路には向かず、年2回ほどの吸引清掃車で泥や落ち葉を吸い取らないと数年で目詰まりを起こすため、適材適所の導入と維持管理が不可欠です。それでも適切な街路に組み合わせれば、透水性舗装は硬い都市の殻を生きた流域へと取り戻してくれます。

passage.text:

It requires a fresh waterproof sealcoat of black tar every two years.
High-suction sweeper trucks loosen coarse stones and must not be used.

items.translation: 第4段落で指摘されている透水性舗装の制約または維持管理上の要件は何ですか。

items.prompt: Cutting maintenance spending may temporarily save money, but it could (     ) the damage to the aging railway.
items.explanation: 保守費削減で老朽鉄道の損傷を悪化させる。
distractorReasons: authenticateは本物と証明する。
exacerbateは悪化させる。
cultivateは育成する。
reimburseは費用を払い戻す。
items.translation: 保守費削減は短期の節約になっても老朽鉄道の損傷を悪化させかねません。

items.prompt: The minister's explanation was subjected to intense (     ) by journalists who questioned every figure.
items.explanation: 数字の一つ一つを疑う厳しい精査。
distractorReasons: courtesyは礼儀。
sympathyは同情。
scrutinyは綿密な調査・精査。
prosperityは繁栄。
items.translation: 大臣の説明は数字を一つずつ疑う記者の厳しい精査を受けました。

items.prompt: The committee gave (     ) approval, reserving the right to reconsider when more evidence became available.
items.explanation: 再検討できる留保付きの暫定承認。
distractorReasons: inherentは本来備わった。
redundantは余分な・不要な。
defiantは反抗的な。
provisionalは暫定的な。
items.translation: 委員会は証拠が増えれば再検討する権利を留保して暫定承認しました。

items.prompt: The negotiator tried to (     ) the conflicting demands of the two groups without dismissing either side.
items.explanation: 対立する要求を調整し両立させる。
distractorReasons: interruptは中断するで要求を調和させる意味でない。
contaminateは汚染する。
reconcileは対立を調和させる。
deteriorateは悪化する。
items.translation: 交渉担当はどちらも退けず両集団の対立する要求を調整しようとしました。

items.prompt: The evidence remains (     ); it is too weak to justify a definite conclusion.
items.explanation: 確定的結論に弱いので決め手に欠ける。
distractorReasons: stringentは「厳格な」で文脈に合わない。
inconclusiveは結論を出せない。
feasibleは「実現可能な」で文脈に合わない。
erraticは「不規則な」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 証拠は依然決め手に欠け、確定的結論を正当化するほど強くありません。

items.prompt: The firm had to write off its investment when the rapid change in technology made its equipment (     ).
items.explanation: 技術変化で設備が時代遅れになった。
distractorReasons: plausibleはもっともらしい。
obsoleteは旧式で使われなくなった。
vigilantは警戒している。
intricateは複雑な。
items.translation: 急速な技術変化で設備が旧式化し、企業は投資額を損失計上せざるを得ませんでした。

items.prompt: The editor rejected the allegation because it was based on (     ) rather than verifiable facts.
items.explanation: 検証できる事実でなく推測に依拠していた。
distractorReasons: standstillは「行き詰まり」で文脈に合わない。
oversightは「監督・見落とし」で文脈に合わない。
conjectureは推測。
moratoriumは「一時停止措置」で文脈に合わない。
items.translation: 編集者は検証可能な事実でなく推測に基づくため申し立てを退けました。

items.prompt: The small hospital proved remarkably (     ), continuing essential services despite repeated power failures.
items.explanation: 停電に耐えて機能を保つ回復力・強さ。
distractorReasons: resilientは困難に強く回復力のある。
superficialは表面的な。
extravagantは浪費的な。
reluctantは気が進まない。
items.translation: 小病院は繰り返す停電にも必須の医療を続け、優れた強靭さを示しました。

items.prompt: The contract contains a (     ) allowing either party to withdraw if the required permit is refused.
items.explanation: 契約内の撤退を認める条項。
distractorReasons: quotaは割当量。
clauseは条項。
tributeは賛辞。
syndromeは症候群。
items.translation: 契約には必要な許可が得られないとき双方に撤退を認める条項があります。

items.prompt: The speaker's claim was met with (     ) because it contradicted well-established observations.
items.explanation: 既存の観察と矛盾し懐疑を招いた。
distractorReasons: nostalgiaは郷愁。
skepticismは懐疑。
hospitalityはもてなし。
ingenuityは創意工夫。
items.translation: 発言者の主張は確立した観察と矛盾していたため懐疑的に受け止められました。

items.prompt: Rather than impose a rigid formula, the policy gives local authorities considerable (     ) in allocating funds.
items.explanation: 硬直した算式でなく資金配分の裁量を認める。
distractorReasons: scarcityは不足。
hostilityは敵意。
erosionは侵食。
discretionは裁量・判断の自由。
items.translation: 政策は硬直した算式を課すのでなく自治体に資金配分の大きな裁量を認めます。

items.prompt: The official tried to (     ) responsibility by blaming a computer error, although he had approved the figures himself.
items.explanation: 自ら承認したのに機械のせいにして責任を回避する。
distractorReasons: retainは保持する。
conferは授与する。
evade responsibilityは責任を逃れる。
endorseは支持する。

items.prompt: A lengthy legal dispute could (     ) the organization's limited resources before the case reaches court.
items.explanation: 長期紛争で限られた資源を使い果たす。
distractorReasons: articulateは明確に述べる。
consolidateは統合・強化する。
reviveは復活させる。
depleteは枯渇させる。

items.prompt: The supposed distinction between the two categories is (     ); the same cases can easily fall into both.
items.explanation: 同じ事例が両方に入るため区別の根拠が恣意的。
distractorReasons: unanimousは全員一致の。
indigenousは土着の。
adjacentは隣接した。
arbitraryは明確な根拠なく恣意的な。

magnifyは拡大するで目的と逆。

A: Several board members questioned the timetable.

passage.title: The Silence in the Archive
passage.text:
Historical collections are sometimes treated as though they were transparent windows onto the past. A researcher asks a question, locates the relevant papers, and extracts an answer. Yet the existence of a document reflects a chain of decisions: someone had to produce it, someone had to retain it, and an institution eventually had to consider it worth preserving. Groups whose daily activities generated few written records may consequently be difficult to study, even when their contribution to a community was substantial.

Consider a project reconstructing the history of a neighborhood market. Official files might contain detailed records of licenses and inspections, while offering almost nothing about informal arrangements through which traders shared transport or helped a sick colleague. If researchers relied exclusively on official files, they could (19). What was easiest to document would acquire disproportionate importance simply because it had survived in an accessible form.

Oral interviews can help broaden such a project, but they do not provide an uncomplicated solution. People may interpret earlier experiences through the concerns of the present. Different accounts may disagree without either speaker deliberately misleading the interviewer. (20), recordings should be accompanied by information about when and under what circumstances they were made. This enables later users to assess the accounts instead of treating them as context-free statements.

An honest archive therefore makes its own limitations visible. It can identify gaps, explain selection policies, and preserve disagreements rather than forcing every account into a single version of events. This does not make historical research impossible. On the contrary, recognizing how a collection was assembled allows researchers to (21). The aim is not to abandon evidence but to ask more precise questions of it.

passage.title: A Standard Is Not a Setting
passage.text:
When a public agency purchases a digital service, adopting a technical standard can appear to resolve the question of accessibility. A supplier certifies that its product complies, the certificate is filed, and the agency proceeds with installation. Standards are indispensable because they establish common expectations that would otherwise have to be negotiated separately for every purchase. However, a certificate describes a product under specified conditions, not every future interaction between that product and its users.

Imagine a booking system that works correctly when tested in isolation. During installation, an agency adds a short time limit, requires documents available only as scanned images, and places essential instructions on another website. Each decision may seem administratively convenient. Taken together, they can create obstacles that were absent from the original test. A compliant product has not necessarily produced (22).

User testing after installation is therefore essential, but it must be organized carefully. Inviting only experienced staff to complete familiar tasks is unlikely to reveal the difficulties faced by someone using assistive technology or encountering the process for the first time. Agencies need feedback from people whose circumstances differ, and a procedure for acting on that feedback. (23), collecting complaints without assigning responsibility for resolving them merely documents exclusion rather than reducing it.

This does not mean that technical standards should be discarded. They provide a necessary baseline and make suppliers accountable for features within their control. The problem arises when meeting a baseline is treated as the end of the agency's responsibility. Accessibility is sustained through procurement, configuration, testing, and maintenance. An effective approach consequently requires agencies to (24), rather than regard accessibility as a property that can be purchased once and then forgotten.
passage.translation: 行政のデジタルサービス調達では、技術標準への適合証明でアクセシビリティ問題が解決したように見えがちです。標準は共通の期待を定めるため不可欠ですが、証明は特定条件下の製品についてで、将来の全利用場面を保証しません。単体試験では正常な予約システムも、導入時に短い制限時間、画像だけの書類、別サイトの重要な説明を加えると障壁を生みます。適合製品が必ずしも(22)を生むわけではありません。導入後の試験も熟練職員だけでは不十分で、支援技術利用者や初回利用者など異なる事情の人の意見と、それに対処する手順が必要です。(23)、解決責任を割り当てず苦情を集めるだけでは排除を記録するにとどまります。標準を廃棄すべきなのでなく、最低基準達成を責任の終点としないことが重要です。調達、設定、試験、保守を通じて(24)必要があります。

passage.title: Who Benefits from a Quieter Street?
passage.text:
Reducing traffic on a residential street may seem an uncomplicated improvement. Fewer vehicles can mean less noise, cleaner air, and more space for people walking or cycling. Yet the evaluation of a traffic scheme depends on where its boundaries are drawn. A street that becomes quieter may sit beside another that receives the diverted vehicles. An assessment limited to the first street can therefore tell a convincing but incomplete story.

Suppose a district introduces barriers that prevent through-traffic from using several residential roads. Initial monitoring shows a sharp decline in vehicles inside the area. Residents living near the barriers report that children can cross more easily and that conversations are no longer interrupted by engine noise. These are genuine benefits, not merely perceptions to be dismissed. However, residents along the main roads outside the area report longer queues. They question why their experience is absent from the first evaluation.

One response is to enlarge the monitoring area. This is necessary, but a larger average alone may still obscure important differences. If a substantial improvement for several thousand people outweighs a smaller deterioration for a few hundred, the overall figure may look favorable. That calculation does not by itself establish whether the distribution of costs is acceptable, especially if those facing deterioration already experience the greatest pollution. Choosing a measurement boundary is therefore not a neutral substitute for considering fairness.

Timing introduces another complication. Drivers may initially follow familiar routes and later change their journey, travel at another hour, or choose another means of transport. The first week may consequently exaggerate permanent disruption. Conversely, waiting for people to adapt cannot justify disregarding persistent problems indefinitely. An evaluation should state in advance when it will be repeated and which findings would trigger a change. Otherwise, every unfavorable result can be described as temporary and every favorable result as final.

A credible process combines measurements with ways for affected people to challenge the interpretation. Residents may identify a school entrance that monitors have missed or explain why a supposedly convenient alternative route is unusable for someone with limited mobility. Their accounts do not replace traffic counts, but they can reveal what the counts fail to capture.

The choice is not simply between accepting every scheme and rejecting any scheme with uneven effects. It is between treating evaluation as a defense of a completed decision and using it to revise that decision. A project can retain its original aims while adding protection for neighboring roads, adjusting delivery access, or removing a barrier that causes disproportionate harm. A quieter street is worth pursuing, but the claim of success becomes stronger when it accounts for people beyond that street.
passage.translation: 住宅街の交通量削減には騒音や空気、歩行環境の改善がありますが、迂回車を受ける周辺道路を評価に含めなければ不完全です。通過交通を防ぐ障壁によって内側の住民は実際に恩恵を受けても、外側の幹線道路の渋滞は最初の評価に表れないことがあります。測定範囲を広げても、平均値は大多数の改善で少数者の悪化を隠しえます。すでに高い汚染にさらされた人に費用が集中する場合、公平さは平均だけで決められません。導入直後と経路・時間・交通手段が適応した後でも結果は異なりますが、適応を口実に永続的な問題を無視することはできません。再評価時期と変更条件を事前に示す必要があります。住民は見落とされた学校入口や移動困難者には使えない代替路を指摘できます。体験談は交通量計測を置き換えず、欠落を発見します。評価は既決定の弁護でなく改善に使うべきで、隣接道路の保護、配送経路の調整、不均衡な害を生む障壁の撤去などで当初の目的を保ちながら修正できます。静かな街路の成功は、その外側の人も考慮するとき、より説得力を持ちます。

passage.title: Who Benefits from a Quieter Street?
passage.text:
Reducing traffic on a residential street may seem an uncomplicated improvement. Fewer vehicles can mean less noise, cleaner air, and more space for people walking or cycling. Yet the evaluation of a traffic scheme depends on where its boundaries are drawn. A street that becomes quieter may sit beside another that receives the diverted vehicles. An assessment limited to the first street can therefore tell a convincing but incomplete story.

Suppose a district introduces barriers that prevent through-traffic from using several residential roads. Initial monitoring shows a sharp decline in vehicles inside the area. Residents living near the barriers report that children can cross more easily and that conversations are no longer interrupted by engine noise. These are genuine benefits, not merely perceptions to be dismissed. However, residents along the main roads outside the area report longer queues. They question why their experience is absent from the first evaluation.

One response is to enlarge the monitoring area. This is necessary, but a larger average alone may still obscure important differences. If a substantial improvement for several thousand people outweighs a smaller deterioration for a few hundred, the overall figure may look favorable. That calculation does not by itself establish whether the distribution of costs is acceptable, especially if those facing deterioration already experience the greatest pollution. Choosing a measurement boundary is therefore not a neutral substitute for considering fairness.

Timing introduces another complication. Drivers may initially follow familiar routes and later change their journey, travel at another hour, or choose another means of transport. The first week may consequently exaggerate permanent disruption. Conversely, waiting for people to adapt cannot justify disregarding persistent problems indefinitely. An evaluation should state in advance when it will be repeated and which findings would trigger a change. Otherwise, every unfavorable result can be described as temporary and every favorable result as final.

A credible process combines measurements with ways for affected people to challenge the interpretation. Residents may identify a school entrance that monitors have missed or explain why a supposedly convenient alternative route is unusable for someone with limited mobility. Their accounts do not replace traffic counts, but they can reveal what the counts fail to capture.

The choice is not simply between accepting every scheme and rejecting any scheme with uneven effects. It is between treating evaluation as a defense of a completed decision and using it to revise that decision. A project can retain its original aims while adding protection for neighboring roads, adjusting delivery access, or removing a barrier that causes disproportionate harm. A quieter street is worth pursuing, but the claim of success becomes stronger when it accounts for people beyond that street.

passage.title: Learning from a Pilot Without Copying It
passage.text:
A successful pilot project is often presented as a miniature version of a future policy. If a service works for a small group, expanding it appears to be a matter of securing enough money and reproducing the same arrangement elsewhere. This picture is appealing to decision-makers because it turns uncertainty into an apparently manageable problem of scale. Unfortunately, the conditions that make a pilot succeed may be precisely those that cannot be reproduced simply by increasing its budget.

Consider a pilot designed to help residents navigate complicated housing applications. A small team operates from a familiar community center, and its coordinator has long-standing relationships with both local families and officials. Staff can telephone a particular official to clarify an unusual case, and residents who distrust formal agencies may approach the coordinator because a neighbor recommends her. None of these features is captured by a description that says only "advice provided at a local center."

When the service is expanded, new offices may be established quickly, but relationships take time. The original coordinator may also have exercised considerable judgment about which rules could be interpreted flexibly and which required strict compliance. A standardized handbook can preserve some of this knowledge, but not necessarily the ability to recognize a new situation. If policymakers copy only the visible procedure, they may reproduce its appearance while losing the mechanisms that made it effective.

This does not render pilots useless. Rather, it changes what should be learned from them. Evaluation needs to identify not only whether an outcome improved but also how the improvement occurred. Were staff reducing delays because they simplified paperwork, because they knew whom to contact, or because the pilot received exceptional attention from senior officials? These explanations imply different prospects for expansion. A process that depends on an unusual level of senior attention may be harder to sustain than one based on a broadly applicable change in application forms.

There is also a danger in selecting only the most enthusiastic communities for a pilot and then treating their results as representative. Such communities may contribute unpaid labor, adapt buildings, or solve problems informally. These contributions can be legitimate strengths of the pilot, but they should not disappear from the account of its costs. Expansion to areas without the same resources may require additional funding or a different design.

A useful next step may therefore be a deliberately varied second trial, rather than immediate nationwide adoption. This trial can test the service in places with different staffing, relationships, and levels of local support. Some adaptations should be permitted, provided the essential mechanism and the reason for each change are documented. Uniformity of every visible detail is not the same as fidelity to the project's purpose.

Ultimately, the most responsible claim for a pilot is rarely that it has eliminated uncertainty. It has made certain assumptions more testable and exposed conditions that deserve attention. Policymakers can then decide which elements should be preserved, which require investment, and which must change. Scaling a project intelligently is a process of learning across settings, not transporting a finished object from one place to another.

passage.title: Adaptive Reuse of Industrial Buildings
passage.text:
Across many cities, former factories and warehouses stand vacant after manufacturing moves elsewhere, leaving large parcels of urban land underused for decades. Instead of demolishing these brick and steel structures and constructing entirely new buildings from scratch, urban planners increasingly favor adaptive reuse, which converts existing industrial shells into public libraries, apartments, or creative offices. Preserving heavy structural frames substantially reduces demolition waste sent to landfills and avoids the significant carbon emissions associated with producing fresh concrete and steel. Equally important, keeping familiar smokestacks or arched windows helps neighborhoods retain their distinctive historical character even as local economies change.

Nevertheless, adaptive reuse is far from effortless in practice. Older industrial buildings were designed for heavy machinery rather than daily human comfort, so they rarely satisfy contemporary standards for thermal insulation, fire exits, acoustic separation, or wheelchair access. Developers also frequently uncover hidden structural deterioration, contaminated soil, or hazardous materials such as asbestos once interior walls are opened, causing renovation budgets and construction schedules to overrun initial estimates.

Specialists therefore emphasize conducting thorough engineering inspections before any conversion is approved, alongside adopting flexible municipal building codes that accommodate historic structures without compromising essential public safety.
passage.translation:
多くの都市で製造業の移転後に旧工場や倉庫が空いたまま残り、広大な都市用地が何十年も十分に活用されない状態にある。都市計画家はこうしたレンガや鉄骨の建物を取り壊してゼロから新築する代わりに、既存の産業建築の躯体を公立図書館や集合住宅、オフィスへ転用する「アダプティブ・リユース（転用改修）」を支持するようになっている。重厚な構造躯体の保存は埋立地へ送られる解体廃棄物を大幅に減らし、新たなコンクリートや鋼材の製造に伴う大量の炭素排出も抑えられる。同様に重要な点として、見慣れた煙突やアーチ窓を残すことで地域経済が変化しても街固有の歴史的個性を保てる。
しかし実務上の転用改修は決して容易ではない。古い産業建築は人間の日常的な快適さではなく重機械のために設計されたため、現代の断熱・避難経路・遮音・バリアフリー基準を満たすことはまれである。内装を解体し始めてから隠れた構造劣化や土壌汚染、アスベストなどの有害物質が見つかり、改修予算や工期が当初の見積もりを超過することも少なくない。
そのため専門家は、転用承認前の綿密な構造調査の実施と、不可欠な公共の安全を損なわずに歴史的建造物へ対応できる柔軟な自治体建築基準の導入を強調している。

items.model: Converting vacant industrial buildings into new public or residential facilities significantly reduces demolition waste and carbon emissions while preserving local architectural heritage. However, renovating older structures often involves unexpected expenses and delays due to strict modern standards, hidden structural damage, and hazardous materials. Consequently, experts recommend comprehensive inspections beforehand and flexible building regulations that maintain essential safety while accommodating historic designs.
items.translation: 空いた産業建築を新たな施設へ転用することは、地域の建築遺産を守りつつ解体廃棄物と炭素排出を減らす。しかし古い建物の改修では、厳格な現代基準や隠れた構造損傷、有害物質のために予想外の費用や遅れが生じやすい。そのため専門家は、綿密な事前調査と、安全性を保ちつつ歴史的構造に対応できる柔軟な建築規則を推奨している。
items.explanation: 第1段落の利点（廃棄物・炭素排出削減と地域景観の維持）、第2段落の課題（現代基準への適合難・隠れた劣化や有害物質による費用と工期の超過）、第3段落の提言（事前調査の徹底と安全性を担保した柔軟な規制）を61語で的確にパラフレーズしています。
rubric: 転用改修の環境面・景観面の利点を自分の言葉で要約した
現代基準・構造劣化・有害物質に伴うコストや遅延の課題を含めた
専門家が求める事前調査と柔軟な規制の必要性を正確に結んだ
主観を交えず60〜70語の厳格な語数範囲に収めた

items.prompt:
次のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。POINTSから2つを選び、序論・本論（2つ）・結論の構成で論述しなさい。（目安語数：120〜150語）
TOPIC: Should governments provide financial incentives for people to move from major cities to rural areas?
POINTS:
• Cost of living
• Employment opportunities
• Local public services
• Infrastructure maintenance
items.model:
I believe governments should provide financial incentives to encourage residents of major cities to relocate to rural communities.
First, such support helps sustain local public services. Many rural towns face rapid population decline, forcing schools, clinics, and bus routes to close. Attracting working-age families increases local tax revenue and demand, making it viable for municipalities to maintain essential services for all residents.
Second, relocation incentives ease the high cost of living experienced in overcrowded metropolitan areas. Housing prices and commuting expenses in major cities place severe financial strain on young households. With initial moving grants and remote-work opportunities, newcomers can secure spacious housing at lower monthly costs while contributing skills to regional businesses.
In conclusion, well-designed relocation subsidies benefit both revitalizing rural regions and overburdened urban households.
items.translation:
私は大都市の住民が地方地域へ移住することを促すため、政府は財政的優遇措置を提供すべきだと考えます。
第一に、そのような支援は地域の公共サービスの維持に役立ちます。多くの地方の町は急速な人口減少に直面し、学校や診療所、バス路線の閉鎖を余儀なくされています。現役世代の世帯を呼び込めば地方税収と需要が増え、自治体が全住民に不可欠なサービスを維持しやすくなります。
第二に、移住支援は過密な大都市圏における高い生活費の負担を和らげます。大都市の住宅価格や通勤費は若い世帯に重い経済的負担を与えています。初期の移住補助金とリモートワークの機会があれば、移住者は毎月の費用を抑えて広い住居を確保しつつ、地域企業に技能で貢献できます。
結論として、適切に設計された移住補助金は、再生を目指す地方と負担の大きい都市世帯の双方に利益をもたらします。
items.explanation: POINTSから「Local public services」と「Cost of living」の2点を選択し、序論（賛成の立場）→本論1（人口減少下の学校・医療・交通維持）→本論2（都市部の住居・通勤コスト緩和とリモートワーク活用）→結論の4段落構成・132語で論理的に展開しています。
rubric: POINTSから2つの観点を明確に選び4段落構成（序論・本論2つ・結論）で論じた
各本論段落で主張→背景・具体説明→帰結の論理展開を行った
準1級にふさわしい語彙・構文を正確に用いた
120〜150語の目安に収まっている

distractorReasons: benignは「良性の、穏やかな」。
affluentは「裕福な」。

items.translation: 調査は、橋の崩落は一度の暴風雨ではなく長年のずさんな保守管理に起因すると結論づけました。

distractorReasons: captivityは「捕虜・飼育状態」。

items.translation: 手頃な保育制度がなければ、地方の雇用を押し上げる取り組みが大きな弾みを得る可能性は低いでしょう。

distractorReasons: emulateは「見習って競う」。

distractorReasons: reconciledは「和解させられた」。

be deceived by ...で「〜に欺かれる、見誤らされる」。

items.translation: 食用キノコと有毒な近縁種が驚くほど似ているため、熟練の植物学者でさえ見誤ることがあります。

distractorReasons: be attributable to ...で「〜に起因する、〜のおかげと考えられる」。

items.prompt: Critics argued that the housing subsidy was merely a (     ) measure that failed to address the shortage of construction workers.

lucidは「明快な」。

provokingは「引き起こす」でFar fromに入れると後半のfueledと逆接にならない。

items.prompt: The archaeological permit was granted on the strict (     ) that every excavated artifact remain in the regional museum.

distractorReasons: complacencyは「自己満足・油断」。
digressionは「脱線」。

items.prompt: Initial enthusiasm for the car-sharing scheme began to (     ) once members realized vehicles were rarely available on weekends.
items.explanation: 週末に車がほとんど借りられないと気づくと、カーシェア制度への当初の熱意が「衰え・薄れ」始めたのでwane。

surgeは「急増する」で逆。

hoistは「巻き上げる」。
items.translation: 週末には車両がめったに空いていないと会員が気づくにつれ、カーシェア制度への当初の熱意は薄れ始めました。

items.prompt: Strict confidentiality rules forbid mediators from revealing anything said during talks, lest trust between the parties (     ).

items.explanation: carve out A from Bは「B（適用対象など）からAを適用除外として切り出す」。小規模農協を大銀行向け規制から除外する文脈に一致（句動詞枠）。

items.explanation: 干ばつのあいだ、秋の収穫まで残りの穀物備蓄を少しずつやりくりして「食い繋ぐ・長持ちさせる」eke out。
